E001.headline: Small drone of unknown origin falls on Przasnysz military base in Poland
E001.description: On 28 January 2026 a small, toy-like drone fell on the military base at Przasnysz, Poland. Its origin is unknown; foreign involvement was not established.
summary: On 28 January 2026 security staff at the military base in Przasnysz, Poland, saw a small, toy-like drone flying over the site before it fell. The incident became public on 2 February 2026, when it was reported that a small drone had fallen on a Polish army base.

The drone’s origin and operator are unknown, and foreign involvement has not been established. Its route before it reached the base is also unknown. It was described as an unsophisticated device, and no recording media were identified on it. An investigation was reported.
No damage or casualties were reported. The drone was secured and handed over to the Military Police.

E002.headline: Drone reported as Russian enters Romanian airspace near Sfântu Gheorghe
E002.description: On 25 February 2026 a drone reported as Russian briefly entered Romanian airspace over territorial waters near Sfântu Gheorghe and Sulina. F-16s were scrambled.
summary: On 25 February 2026 radar detected a drone entering Romanian airspace over territorial waters near Sfântu Gheorghe, in Tulcea, during attacks on Ukrainian ports on the Danube. The drone left it north of Sulina. The incursion was confirmed as short; one earlier report put it at about 20 minutes, but that figure is unverified and the exact duration has not been established.
The drone was reported as Russian, and Romania’s defence ministry (MApN) connected the incident to Russian strikes on Ukraine. Its model is unknown.
Two F-16 fighter jets were scrambled at 17:50 local time, and an RO-Alert warning was issued at 18:07. The alert ended at about 18:45. No harm or debris was reported.

E003.headline: Swedish military links drone near French carrier off Malmö to Russian ship
E003.description: In February 2026 a drone flew near the carrier Charles de Gaulle in the Öresund off Malmö, Sweden. Swedish forces blamed a Russian ship; Russia rejected it.
summary: In late February 2026 the Swedish naval vessel HMS Rapp detected a drone in the Öresund off Malmö, Sweden, during a visit by the French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle. The drone flew near the area protecting the carrier. Accounts differ on the date: an earlier report gave 26 February, while an account citing the Swedish military dates the encounter to 25 February.

The Swedish military attributed the launch to the Russian intelligence ship Zhigulevsk, which was transiting the Öresund, and technical data were reported to link the launch to the ship. Russia rejected the allegation. The drone’s model has not been conclusively identified.

The Swedish vessel jammed or disrupted the drone, but its final fate is unknown and no shoot-down has been confirmed. No casualties were reported, and the carrier’s operations were reportedly unaffected. France commented on the incident on 27 February 2026.

E004.headline: Military drone found at mine near Konin, Poland, probably from 2025 flight
E004.description: On 12 March 2026 a military drone was found at a mine near Konin, Poland. It was reported as probably Russian and probably linked to a September 2025 incursion.
summary: On 12 March 2026 a military drone was found at a lignite mine near Konin, in the Mniszków–Gałczyce area of Greater Poland. A mine employee reportedly came across it, and it may have been lying there for months. The date is that of the discovery, not of a flight: no 2026 flight has been established.

The drone was reported as probably Russian. On 13 March Poland’s defence minister linked it to a drone incursion in September 2025, describing the connection as probable rather than proven. The drone’s model was not specified.
No harm was reported. Police and the Military Police investigated the find.

E005.headline: Drone that crashed on Lake Lavysas identified as Ukrainian by Lithuania
E005.description: On 23 March 2026 a military drone crashed on frozen Lake Lavysas in Varėna district, Lithuania. Lithuania’s government identified it as Ukrainian.
summary: On 23 March 2026 a military drone came down on the ice-covered Lake Lavysas in the Varėna district of Lithuania, roughly 20 km from the border with Belarus. An explosion was reported, and the wreckage was found on the frozen lake.

On 24 March the Lithuanian government identified the drone as Ukrainian. It was reported to have been intended for an attack on oil-export facilities at Primorsk before it went astray. An explanation involving electronic warfare remains an assessment rather than an established finding. The drone carried a military payload, but the exact charge was not specified.
No casualties were reported. The site was secured and the wreckage was examined.

E006.headline: Drone that hit Auvere power station identified as Ukrainian by Estonia
E006.description: On 25 March 2026 a drone that entered Estonia from Russia hit a chimney at the Auvere power station. Estonian authorities said the drone was Ukrainian.
summary: On the morning of 25 March 2026 a military drone hit a chimney of the Auvere power station in Ida-Viru County, Estonia. The drone had entered Estonia from Russia.

Estonian authorities said the drone was Ukrainian. Its intended target was reported to be in Russia, not Estonia. The incident was treated as spillover from the war, and an intentional attack on Estonia has not been established.

No injuries were reported, and there were no reports of any interruption to the plant’s operations. Authorities examined the impact site and the wreckage. A stray drone was also reported in Latvia the same day, and the Baltic defence ministers issued a joint statement on the drone incidents.

E007.headline: Latvian president says drone that crashed near Krāslava was Ukrainian
E007.description: On 25 March 2026 a military drone crashed in the Krāslava region of Latvia. Latvia’s president said it was Ukrainian; it had entered via Russian airspace.
summary: On the morning of 25 March 2026 a military drone crashed in a rural area of the Krāslava region of Latvia. One additional account, from the Centre for Eastern Studies (OSW), places the crash at Dobročina.

Latvia’s president said the drone was Ukrainian. It entered Latvia through Russian airspace during Ukrainian strikes on targets in Russia. Why it came down in Latvia, whether through malfunction or diversion, has not been demonstrated.

No casualties were reported. Latvian authorities recovered and investigated the wreckage. A stray drone was also reported in Estonia the same day, and the Baltic defence ministers issued a joint statement on the drone incidents.

E008.headline: Drone of unidentified operator crosses Latvia from Belarus to Russia
E008.description: On 25 March 2026 Latvia reported a drone briefly crossing eastern Latvia from Belarus into Russia. Its nationality and operator were not identified.
summary: On 25 March 2026 Latvian authorities reported that an additional drone had briefly crossed Latvian territory, entering from Belarus and leaving into Russia. The exact track it took through Latvia was not specified.

The drone’s nationality and operator were not stated, and its model is unknown. Reporting established that it entered Latvia from abroad, but no wreckage and no public identification of the operator were reported.
The drone was monitored and no engagement was reported. No harm was reported. It was reported as a separate flight from the military drone that crashed in Latvia’s Krāslava region the same day.

E009.headline: At least two drones crash near Kouvola, Finland, at least one Ukrainian
E009.description: On 29–30 March 2026 at least two drones came down in southeast Finland, including north of Kouvola. At least one was identified as Ukrainian.
summary: Reports covering 29–30 March 2026 said that at least two drones had entered Finland and come down in the southeast of the country, including north of Kouvola. The exact date and site for each drone have not been resolved. Finnish F/A-18 fighters were deployed, and a pilot reportedly held fire because of the risk on the ground.

At least one of the drones was identified as Ukrainian, and at least one as an AN-196, but the attribution of each object is not equally established. The drones were reported to have strayed during attacks on targets in Russia, and interference was considered a possible cause; that electronic-warfare explanation is not a forensic certainty.
No casualties were reported. Finland investigated the incident as a territorial violation, and wreckage was recovered.

E010.headline: Drone detections and debris finds in Estonia’s Tartu County and Finland
E010.description: On 31 March–1 April 2026 drones and debris were reported in Tartu County, Estonia, with a separate find in Finland. Estonia assessed its cases as Ukrainian.
summary: Between 31 March and 1 April 2026 drone detections and suspected incursions were reported in Tartu County, Estonia, and debris was found at a separate, unspecified site in Finland’s border area. These dates mark a reporting window, not precise crash dates, and the number of objects involved is unresolved.

Estonia assessed the drones in its case as Ukrainian drones intended for Russia, and reporting associated the border activity with further strikes in Russia. Attribution has not been established for every find in Finland. The available detail is not enough to match each track to each recovered object, so it is not known whether the sightings involved one drone or several.
No casualties were reported. Military and border authorities carried out searches and a technical examination of the finds.

E011.headline: Drone reported as Russian crashes in Galați, Romania, damaging property
E011.description: On 25 April 2026 a military drone reported as Russian crashed in Bariera Traian, Galați, Romania, damaging a pole and a building. Its explosives were destroyed.
summary: On 25 April 2026 a military drone crashed in the Bariera Traian area of Galați, Romania. It reportedly approached at low altitude over Lake Brateș, although its precise track has not been independently reconstructed. The drone damaged an electricity pole and a household or workshop structure.

Contemporaneous coverage of the explosive disposal reported the drone as Russian. Its model was not specified. RAF Typhoon fighters had been scrambled for threats nearby, but this drone was not shot down.

Explosive material was confirmed in the drone, and the recovered explosives were detonated in a controlled disposal the same day. The crash caused property damage, but no casualties were reported. It is a separate incident from a drone impact on an apartment building in Galați on 29 May 2026.

E012.headline: Drone fragments found near farm at Văcăreni, Romania; operator unknown
E012.description: On 25 April 2026 drone fragments were found near a farm at Văcăreni, Tulcea County, Romania. A foreign military link was reported, but the operator is unknown.
summary: On 25 April 2026 drone fragments were found near a farm close to Văcăreni, in Tulcea County, Romania. The date is that of the discovery, not of a flight: when the drone flew or came down, and by what route, is unknown, as is the number of drones the fragments came from.
Reporting associated the fragments with a foreign military drone, but the exact operator has not been established.

No casualties were reported. The area was investigated, and specialists collected and reviewed the fragments. The next day, further fragments with an explosive charge were reported between Luncavița and Văcăreni. Romanian reporting distinguished the two finds, but it has not been shown whether they came from the same drone or from different ones.

E013.headline: Drone fragments with explosive charge destroyed near Luncavița, Romania
E013.description: On 26 April 2026 drone fragments with an explosive charge were found between Luncavița and Văcăreni, Romania, and destroyed. Their origin is being investigated.
summary: On 26 April 2026 further drone fragments were reported between Luncavița and Văcăreni in Tulcea County, Romania, a day after fragments were found near a farm at Văcăreni. An explosive charge was confirmed among the material, and an RO-Alert safety warning was issued.

The provenance of the fragments is under investigation, and an investigation by prosecutors at the Constanța Court of Appeal was reported. When the drone flew or came down is unknown. The fragments are not confirmed as a second complete drone, and it has not been established whether they and the previous day’s find came from one airframe or more.

Pyrotechnicians from the SRI and specialists from Romania’s defence ministry (MApN) assessed the material, which was then destroyed in a controlled detonation on site under the prosecutor’s authority. No casualties were reported.

E014.headline: Drone of unknown origin found near Șerbăuți in Suceava County, Romania
E014.description: On 3 May 2026 a drone was found near Șerbăuți, Suceava County, Romania, about 20 km from Ukraine. Its operator and nationality have not been established.
summary: On 3 May 2026 a drone was found in a rural area near Șerbăuți in Suceava County, Romania, around 20 km from Ukraine, near Romania’s northern border. The date is when the drone was found and reported. When it actually came down, and the route it took to get there, are unknown.
The available accounts do not establish the drone’s nationality or its operator, and its model was not specified. Its identity and provenance remain unresolved.
No harm was reported. Romanian authorities investigated the find, and the drone was recovered.

E015.headline: Suspected drone incursion reported at Virolahti in southeastern Finland
E015.description: On 3 May 2026 a suspected drone was tracked in border airspace at Virolahti, southeastern Finland, and reportedly left toward Russia. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 3 May 2026 a drone track was reported in the border airspace at Virolahti in southeastern Finland. The object, described as a suspected drone, was reported to have left in the direction of Russia.
The object’s origin and model have not been resolved, and its attribution remains open. The case was treated as a suspected violation of Finnish territory rather than a confirmed one.
No impact was reported. The track was monitored and the incident was investigated.

E016.headline: Three drones enter Latvia; two crash, one damaging oil tanks at Rēzekne
E016.description: On 7 May 2026 three drones entered Latvia from Russian airspace; two crashed, one damaging empty oil tanks at Rēzekne. Later reports linked them to Ukraine.
summary: On 7 May 2026 three drones entered Latvia from Russian airspace over the Balvi, Ludza and Rēzekne area. Two crashed and one left Latvia. One of the impacts affected an oil-storage site at Rēzekne, where four empty oil tanks were damaged and a fire broke out. Explosive effects were reported, but the exact charges are unknown.

The drones’ technical origin was initially unresolved; later reporting associated the incidents with Ukrainian strike drones. Latvia’s defence ministry discussed Russian electronic warfare as a possible cause. A military and police investigation followed, with criminal proceedings under Chapter 10 of the Latvian Criminal Law.

No casualties were reported. NATO aircraft were deployed and mobile alerts were issued. Wreckage was recovered from one crash site while another was still being searched for. After the oil-tank impacts, the Baltic states sought more NATO defence.

E017.headline: Military sea drone found in Lefkada cave, Greece; Ukraine denies ownership
E017.description: On 7 May 2026 a fisherman found a sea drone with explosives in a cave on Lefkada, Greece. Greek officials called it Ukrainian-built; Ukraine denied ownership.
summary: On 7 May 2026 a fisherman found a military unmanned surface vessel, or sea drone, in a coastal cave on the Greek island of Lefkada. He reportedly moved or towed the vessel before the authorities secured it. Explosives were reported on the drone.

Greek officials described the sea drone as Ukrainian-built or of a Ukrainian type. Ukraine denied ownership, and ownership remains disputed. Its launch point and route are unknown. A later Greek investigation, reported on 15 May, considered that it may have suffered a technical failure or travelled off course.
No casualties were reported. The Coast Guard, police and Navy investigated, the vessel was transferred to a naval facility, and the explosives were later destroyed in a controlled disposal.

E018.headline: Suspected drone alert suspends Helsinki airport activity in Finland
E018.description: On 15 May 2026 suspected drones near Helsinki, Finland, prompted a stay-indoors warning and halted airport activity. Their foreign origin was not proven.
summary: On 15 May 2026 suspected drone activity in the Helsinki metropolitan area of Finland triggered broad protective measures. Residents were warned to stay indoors, activity at the airport was suspended and fighter jets were scrambled. How many drones were involved, and of what type, has not been resolved.

Foreign origin has not been proven, and the route of any drones is unknown. Finnish authorities assessed the threat, and their statement at the time did not confirm a direct military threat. The episode was an alert and disruption, not a confirmed attack.
No physical harm was reported.

E019.headline: Wreckage of suspected Ukrainian drone found near Utena, Lithuania
E019.description: On 17 May 2026 wreckage of a suspected Ukrainian military drone was found near Samanė and Utena, Lithuania, and explosives were then found nearby.
summary: On 17 May 2026 wreckage of a suspected military drone was found in the Samanė and Utena area of Lithuania, and explosive material was then found nearby, with follow-up reports on 18 May. The date is that of the discovery: the drone’s flight path is unknown, and it has not been established that it crashed or exploded on that day.

The drone was suspected to be Ukrainian, but this was not stated as a final forensic identification, and its technical identification was reported to be under investigation. The explosives are linked to the same wreckage and are not taken to indicate a second drone.
No injuries were reported. Authorities cordoned off the site, recovered the material and investigated.

E020.headline: Drone of unknown origin enters Latvian airspace near Russian border
E020.description: On 17 May 2026 a drone was reported entering and leaving Latvian airspace near the Russian border. Its operator and model are unknown; its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 17 May 2026 a drone was reported to have entered Latvian airspace near the border with Russia and later to have left it. The Latvian military reportedly tracked the temporary incursion. The precise location of the incursion has not been established.
The drone’s operator and model are unknown, and it has not been finally identified. Any link to Ukraine rests only on suspicion drawn from the wider context, not on an identification of this drone.
The drone was monitored and no shoot-down was reported. No damage or other impact was reported.

E021.headline: Drone shot down over Estonia’s Põltsamaa area identified as Ukrainian
E021.description: On 19 May 2026 a Romanian F-16 under NATO command shot down a drone over the Põltsamaa area of Estonia. Estonia said it was Ukrainian; Kyiv apologized.
summary: On 19 May 2026 a drone entered Estonian airspace and was shot down over the Kablaküla and Põltsamaa area of Estonia. A NATO fighter tracked the incoming drone, and a Romanian F-16 operating under NATO command shot it down. The debris was investigated.

Estonia said the drone was Ukrainian, and Kyiv apologized. The drone was reported to have been intended for a target in Russia. Ukraine said Russian electronic warfare had diverted it; that explanation is Ukraine’s own account.
No civilian harm was reported. An air alert in eastern Latvia the same day may have been part of the same wave, but it has not been established that a second drone was involved.

E022.headline: Air alert in eastern Latvia possibly linked to drone downed over Estonia
E022.description: On 19 May 2026 an air alert in eastern Latvia disrupted trains and exams. It may be linked to a drone shot down over Estonia; no separate drone was established.
summary: On 19 May 2026 an air alert was issued in eastern Latvia. Civil warnings and shelter measures followed, along with a NATO response. Train services and exams were disrupted, and some shops reportedly closed. The exact locations affected have not been established.

The alert came on the same day that a drone reported as Ukrainian was downed over Estonia, and it may have been part of the same wave. The origin of whatever triggered the alert, and its relationship to the Estonian drone, remain unresolved. Open reporting did not establish whether a separate object entered Latvia, and no distinct drone has been identified.

E023.headline: Suspected drone alert disrupts Vilnius airport and rail in Lithuania
E023.description: On 20 May 2026 a suspected drone triggered an air-danger warning in Vilnius, Lithuania, disrupting the airport and rail. Its origin has not been established.
summary: On 20 May 2026 an air-danger warning linked to a suspected drone (UAV) was issued for Vilnius, Lithuania, and its surrounding airspace. The warning, which included a call to shelter, triggered protective closures in the capital. The airport, rail services, the parliament and schools were reportedly disrupted, and authorities imposed temporary traffic restrictions.

How many suspected drones were involved, and of what model, was not specified, and the route is unknown. Who operated the drone, and from which country it came, has not been established; no final attribution has been made.
No confirmed impact was reported.

E024.headline: Reported drone incursion prompts shelter warning on Latvia's eastern border
E024.description: On 21 May 2026 at least one drone was reported over Latvia's eastern border regions. NATO fighters were launched; the drone's origin has not been established.
summary: On 21 May 2026 an air threat was reported in Latvian municipalities along the eastern border, in regions adjoining Belarus and Russia. At least one drone (UAV) was reported in Latvian airspace, and residents were instructed to shelter.
The drone's operator and model are unknown. One account described it entering from Belarus, but its origin has not been established and its final identity remains unresolved.
NATO fighters were launched in response. No impact was confirmed.

E025.headline: Suspected aerial objects prompt NATO response in Utena County, Lithuania
E025.description: On 21 May 2026 two suspected aerial objects in Utena County, Lithuania, drew warnings and a NATO aircraft response. Their identity and origin are unconfirmed.
summary: On 21 May 2026 two suspected aerial objects were detected in the airspace over Utena County, Lithuania. Warnings were issued and NATO aircraft were reported to have responded.
It has not been definitively established that the objects were drones (UAVs), or that they came from abroad. Findings on the individual objects were not available, and their route was not specified.
No physical harm was reported. The detection is treated as a single incident involving two objects, not as two confirmed foreign-drone incursions.

E026.headline: Drone of unknown origin falls into Lake Drīdzis in Latvia and explodes
E026.description: On 23 May 2026 locals reported a drone falling into Lake Drīdzis in Krāslava municipality, Latvia, then an explosion. Its origin has not been established.
summary: On the morning of 23 May 2026 local residents reported a drone falling into Lake Drīdzis, in Kombuļi parish, Krāslava municipality, Latvia. The report came at around 08:00 local time, which is not necessarily the exact time of the crash. An explosion was observed; the type of charge is unknown.

The drone's nationality and operator are unknown. It was reported to have arrived from a direction near Belarus, but no attribution has been established. Sensors reportedly registered no breach beforehand, and the origin was under investigation.
No casualties were reported. The State Police, rescuers with a boat and the armed forces searched the lake, and possible debris was located.

E027.headline: Homemade smuggling drone forced down near Belarus border in Lithuania
E027.description: On 23 May 2026 a homemade cargo drone reported arriving from Belarus was forced down and seized at Dumblė, Šalčininkai district, Lithuania, in a smuggling case.
summary: On 23 May 2026 a homemade cargo drone carrying smuggled goods was reportedly forced down at Dumblė, in Lithuania's Šalčininkai district on the border with Belarus. Border enforcement officers intercepted the drone and seized it.

The drone was reported to have arrived from Belarus. It was a criminal smuggling flight, not a military one, and the operator has not been identified. Details of the cargo and of the drone itself were not available.
No explosive payload and no casualties were reported. Reports describe a forced landing and seizure, not a shoot-down or a crash.

E028.headline: Romania says Russian drone hit Galați apartment block, injuring two
E028.description: Overnight on 29 May 2026 a drone hit an apartment block in Galați, Romania, injuring two. Romanian authorities identified it as Russian; Moscow disputed this.
summary: Overnight on 29 May 2026 a drone struck the roof of an apartment block in the Mazepa district of Galați, Romania, and started a fire. Two people suffered minor injuries, residents were evacuated and homes were damaged. Officials estimated that the drone carried at least 30 kg of explosives.

Based on an official radar and debris assessment, Romanian authorities identified it as a Russian Geran-2 drone. It was associated with a wider wave of 43 drones in attacks on Ukraine and made a brief flight over Romania before the impact. Moscow disputed the attribution. Romania did not describe the strike as an intentional attack directed at Romania.

Two Romanian F-16s and a helicopter were scrambled but did not engage over the city, and the site was examined. The Russian consul was expelled and the consulate closed in response. The incident is separate from a drone crash in Galați on 25 April 2026.

E029.headline: Suspected drone activity triggers alerts on Latvian and Estonian borders
E029.description: Overnight on 3 June 2026 suspected drones triggered alerts in eastern border regions of Latvia and Estonia. NATO fighters responded; origin is unconfirmed.
summary: Overnight on 3 June 2026 suspected drone (UAV) activity triggered alerts in the eastern border regions of both Latvia and Estonia. Civil warnings were issued and NATO fighters responded. Precise flight tracks were not published.
The number and identity of the objects remain unresolved. A foreign origin was suspected but has not been established for each object, and no wreckage or definitive attribution has been reported.
No impact or casualties were confirmed. The alerts in the two countries are treated as one cross-border cluster, because individual tracks cannot be counted reliably.

E030.headline: Sea drone reaches Constanța port in Romania and later self-detonates
E030.description: On 5 June 2026 a sea drone of a type used by Ukraine reached Constanța port, Romania, and later self-detonated. Ukraine blamed its drift on Russian jamming.
summary: On the morning of 5 June 2026 an uncrewed sea drone (USV) was found in Constanța port, Romania, near the oil-terminal and berth area, after reportedly moving off course into the port. It later self-detonated. Other detonations were reported nearby, and further sea drones were reported in offshore waters; their number has not been established.

The drone was of a type used by Ukraine. Ukraine attributed its drift to Russian jamming. The exact operators, the number of separate offshore vehicles and the mechanisms involved have not been fully established.

Port and security authorities secured the area, and the military and coast guard intervened. No casualties or major additional damage were reported. The port is Romanian sovereign territory; jurisdiction over the nearby offshore waters varies.

E031.headline: French NATO fighter shoots down drone near Bērzgale, Latvia
E031.description: On 8 June 2026 a French NATO fighter shot down a drone in Latvian airspace near Bērzgale, Latvia. Its nationality and model were not conclusively identified.
summary: On 8 June 2026 a drone (UAV) entered Latvian airspace and was intercepted in the Bērzgale area of Latvia. A French fighter jet operating with NATO then shot it down.

The drone's nationality and model were not conclusively identified in contemporaneous accounts of the incident. It is treated as a foreign drone, but its origin has not been established; its route was not specified, and what, if anything, it carried remains unknown.
No casualties were reported in Latvia. After the shoot-down, a search for the wreckage and an investigation of the debris followed.

E032.headline: Romania destroys drone fragments near Rachelu it identified as Russian
E032.description: On 30 June 2026 the Romanian military destroyed drone fragments near Rachelu, Tulcea County, Romania. The defence ministry identified them as Russian.
summary: On 30 June 2026 the Romanian military carried out a controlled detonation of drone fragments near Rachelu, in Tulcea County, Romania. The recovered material posed an explosive hazard, of an unspecified size, and required explosive-ordnance disposal. 30 June is the disposal date: when the drone flew, and when the fragments were found, has not been established.
Romania's Ministry of Defence identified the fragments as belonging to a Russian drone. The drone's original route is unspecified and the individual airframe has not been identified.
No casualties were reported. The disposal is treated as a recovery of wreckage, not as a separately demonstrated new incursion into Romania.

E033.headline: LPG ship crew report drone attack off Sfântu Gheorghe, Romania
E033.description: On 21 July 2026 explosions badly damaged an LPG ship in the Black Sea off Sfântu Gheorghe, Romania. Crew described three drones; a drone cause is unconfirmed.
summary: During the night and morning of 21 July 2026 explosions badly damaged an LPG-carrying merchant ship in the Black Sea, about 26 km off Sfântu Gheorghe, Romania, and the vessel caught fire. The position was reported to be outside Romania's territorial waters.

Two crew members described a night-time attack by three drones. Their account is treated as an allegation, not a final identification of the weapon: the drone type, the devices and charges used, the launch point and the operator or nationality have not been identified, and a drone cause has not been confirmed.

Romanian maritime rescue services intervened and brought the crew to safety. Injuries were reported, including burns. The incident is separate from a bulk carrier's emergency off the same coast on 24 July and from the Progress IV incident in August.

E034.headline: Bulk carrier Christina B damaged off Romania; mine or drone unresolved
E034.description: On 24 July 2026 the bulk carrier Christina B was damaged in Romania's Black Sea EEZ off Sfântu Gheorghe. Whether a mine or a sea drone hit it is unresolved.
summary: On 24 July 2026 the Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Christina B, a coal carrier reportedly sailing from the USA to Ukraine, issued an emergency call after a possible explosive impact in the Black Sea. The ship was about 22 miles off Sfântu Gheorghe, in Romania's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and outside Romanian sovereign territorial waters.

It has not been established whether the ship struck a mine or was hit by a maritime drone. The device and the mechanism of the explosion are unidentified, drone involvement has not been confirmed, and the origin and operator remain unresolved.
The ship was damaged; no injuries were reported. Romanian maritime authorities responded, and the vessel was assessed for onward movement or repairs.

E035.headline: Romania shoots down drone it identified as Russian over Buzău County
E035.description: On 24 July 2026 a Romanian F-16 shot down a Shahed-type drone over Padina–Pogoanele, Buzău County, Romania. Romanian authorities identified it as Russian.
summary: On 24 July 2026 a Romanian F-16 shot down a drone over an uninhabited part of the Padina–Pogoanele area in Buzău County, Romania. The drone had approached from the Black Sea and Danube area and then flown a long way inland. Italian NATO aircraft and Romanian aircraft responded before it was destroyed.

Romanian authorities identified it as a Russian drone. It was described as Shahed-type, but its exact designation has not been conclusively established, and details of its type and precise track rest on secondary reporting. The wreckage was under investigation.
No casualties were reported.

E036.headline: Romanian fighter downs drone reported as Russian over Tulcea coast
E036.description: On 25 July 2026 a Romanian fighter shot down a drone reported as Russian after a brief incursion over the Sfântu Gheorghe and Tulcea coast of Romania.
summary: On 25 July 2026 a drone (UAV) made a brief incursion into Romanian airspace over the Sfântu Gheorghe and Tulcea coastal sector and was destroyed by a Romanian fighter jet. It had made a short entry from the operational area of the war in Ukraine. Fragments were sought afterwards.
The drone was reported as Russian. Its model and payload were under investigation, and its technical identification had not been completed in contemporary accounts.
No casualties were reported.

E037.headline: Romania shoots down drone it identified as Russian off Sulina
E037.description: On 26 July 2026 a Romanian F-16 shot down a drone over territorial waters 12 km northeast of Sulina. Romania identified it as Russian, the third in three days.
summary: On 26 July 2026 a drone (UAV) approaching from the Black Sea was shot down by a Romanian F-16 over Romanian territorial waters, about 12 km northeast of Sulina, Romania. It was the third drone Romania had destroyed on three successive days.
Romania identified it as a Russian drone. Its model was not specified, and the investigation into its model and payload had not been completed when the incident was reported.
No casualties were reported. An ambassador was summoned over the repeated violations.

E038.headline: Drone reported as Russian briefly enters southeastern Romania
E038.description: On 27 July 2026 a drone reported as Russian briefly entered southeastern Romanian airspace and left for Ukraine before it was engaged. No impact was reported.
summary: On 27 July 2026 a drone (UAV) was reported to have made a brief incursion into Romania's southeastern airspace before exiting into Ukraine. Its exact route was not specified. Romanian air defences monitored and responded to the flight, but the drone departed before it could be engaged.

The drone was reported as Russian, but details of the incident are limited: no technical findings were available, and the drone's model and payload were not reported. No impact was reported in Romania.

E039.headline: Drone debris falls near Periprava, Romania, after reported interception
E039.description: On 2 August 2026 a drone linked to attacks on Ukraine left Romanian airspace, was reportedly intercepted in Ukraine, and debris fell near Periprava, Romania.
summary: On the afternoon of 2 August 2026 a drone (UAV) was detected over the Sulina branch near Periprava, Tulcea County, Romania, at 15:09 local time. Romanian F-16s were scrambled at 15:17 and monitored it. The drone flew on into Ukraine, where it was reportedly destroyed by Ukrainian forces, and debris fell back into a field near the border at Periprava. The alert ended at 16:05.

The drone was associated with attacks on Ukraine; its final model has not been established. Romania's defence ministry (MApN) reported the flight and the recovery, via HotNews. An interception and debris fall were reported, but it has not been explicitly established that the drone was shot down.
No casualties or property damage were reported. The field was searched and the material investigated.

E040.headline: Germany links Leipzig airport drone to people acting for Russian agencies
E040.description: On 4–5 August 2026 an explosive drone's charge failed at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Germany. Germany blamed people acting for Russian agencies; Russia denied it.
summary: Overnight on 4–5 August 2026 a drone carrying professional explosives and a detonator reached Leipzig/Halle Airport at Schkeuditz, Germany, but the charge failed. The airport was disrupted. Separately, a cargo aircraft reported encountering an object in a suspected collision and diverted to Hanover; minor aircraft damage was reported, but the object was not conclusively identified as a drone. On 14 August a further suspected attack drone was found near Kabelsketal; the find was reported on 25 August, and the object was reportedly associated with about 50 g of suspected RDX.

On 1 September Germany attributed the operation to persons acting for Russian state agencies. Russia denied responsibility. The attribution has not been accompanied by public release of all the underlying forensic and intelligence evidence, and the launch point has not been established.
No casualties were reported. Police, bomb-disposal teams with a robot and federal prosecutors investigated, the additional device was seized, and diplomatic measures followed later.

E041.headline: Two drones sighted over military installation in western Germany
E041.description: On the night of 7–8 August 2026 two drones were sighted over a military installation in western Germany. No foreign or Russian link has been established.
summary: On the night of 7–8 August 2026 two drones were seen above a military installation in western Germany. The precise site was not specified, and the sighting was reported on 8 August. The drones' launch points are unknown.
No foreign or Russian link has been established.
No damage or casualties were reported. Authorities investigated the overflight of the sensitive site.

E042.headline: Drone assessed as Ukrainian type crashes and explodes at Kardam, Bulgaria
E042.description: On 8 August 2026 a drone reported as a Maya-type decoy crashed and exploded in a field at Kardam, Bulgaria. It was assessed as a Ukrainian type; unconfirmed.
summary: On 8 August 2026 a drone crashed and exploded in a sunflower field at Kardam, Bulgaria, near the Romanian border and close to gas infrastructure. It was reported to have flown through Romania and Bulgaria before the crash. No casualties or significant damage to infrastructure were reported.

The drone was reported as a Maya-type decoy and was assessed in earlier reporting as a Ukrainian type, but its final attribution has not been independently established. An explosive effect was observed, though the drone's exact configuration is unknown. By 26 August a Bulgarian minister said Ukraine had not provided the information requested; military prosecutors in Sliven are responsible for the case.

Bulgaria investigated, and additional counter-drone defensive measures were reported. The flight through Romania and the crash in Bulgaria are treated as one incident, not as separate Romanian and Bulgarian incidents.

E043.headline: Romanian Navy destroys two drifting Gerbera drones near Neptun Deep
E043.description: On 11 August 2026 two Gerbera drones found drifting near Neptun Deep, 90 nautical miles off Constanța in Romania's EEZ, were destroyed. Operator unconfirmed.
summary: On the morning of 11 August 2026 a civilian vessel reported two aerial drones drifting at sea near the Neptun Deep works area, about 90 nautical miles off Constanța. The area lies in Romania's exclusive economic zone (EEZ), not in its territorial sea. A separate drone wing was also found; it has not been shown to come from a third drone.

The drones were identified as Gerbera aerial drones, a type used by Russia. Ukraine said the objects were not Ukrainian. No operator has been conclusively established, and the drones' original flight routes are unknown.

Romanian Navy divers and explosive-ordnance disposal specialists, supported by the Coast Guard, destroyed the two drones, which posed a potential explosive hazard, and recovered the wing, which was reported to be non-hazardous. No casualties were reported. These were aerial drones floating at sea, not uncrewed surface vessels, and they are separate from a sea-drone case on 20 August.

E044.headline: Latvia says drone shot down near Rugāji by Italian jet was Ukrainian
E044.description: On 14 August 2026 an Italian NATO Eurofighter shot down a drone near Rugāji, Latvia. On 20 August Latvia confirmed the drone was of Ukrainian origin.
summary: Early on 14 August 2026 an incoming drone (UAV) was shot down by an Italian Eurofighter flying with NATO near Rugāji, in Latvia's Balvi municipality, about 35 km from the Russian border. Troops then searched for the wreckage.

The drone was initially unidentified. On 20 August Latvia confirmed that it was of Ukrainian origin. It may have entered Latvia from Belarus, and Russian electronic interference was considered, but neither has been independently established.
No casualties were reported. The 20 August identification was an update on the same incident, not a second incursion.

E045.headline: Spanish NATO jet downs drone reported as Russian near Galați, Romania
E045.description: On 16 August 2026 a Spanish F/A-18 assigned to NATO shot down a drone between Băleni and Cudalbi, Galați County, Romania. It was reported as Russian.
summary: On 16 August 2026 a drone was shot down between Băleni and Cudalbi in Galați County, Romania, about 24 km from Galați. It had reportedly entered Romanian airspace through Moldova. A Spanish F/A-18 fighter assigned to NATO engaged it above an uninhabited area.

The drone was reported as Russian, and a NATO account described its origin as apparently Russian. Earlier reporting gave its type as Geran-2, but its exact type has not been independently verified. The shoot-down itself has been confirmed.
No casualties were reported, and no payload details were given. The wreckage was recovered and investigated.

E046.headline: Drone tracked into Romania crashes northeast of Grindu, Tulcea County
E046.description: On 20 August 2026 a drone entered Romanian airspace east of Galați and crashed near Grindu, Tulcea County. Its model and operator were not specified.
summary: In the early hours of 20 August 2026 a drone crashed about 4 km northeast of Grindu, in Tulcea County, Romania. According to the Romanian Ministry of National Defence, a group of drones was detected near Ukraine at 02:23 and a warning was issued at 03:20; one drone entered Romanian airspace about 13 km east of Galați at 03:21 and crashed at 03:24. The warning ended at 03:52 local time.
The drone was associated with attacks across the Danube, but the ministry’s initial release did not specify its model or operator, and a complete forensic result is not available.

It burned briefly after the crash and the fire went out on its own; no casualties or property damage were reported. Spanish F-18 fighters and a Romanian IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter responded, followed by a search and a technical examination. An earlier report said the recovered fragments posed no explosive hazard, which the initial release did not confirm. The crash is separate from the sea drone reported near Neptun Deep the same day.

E047.headline: Romanian F-16 fires on explosive naval drone near Neptun Deep works
E047.description: On 20 August 2026 a Romanian F-16 damaged an explosive sea drone near Neptun Deep, in Romania’s EEZ, before the Navy neutralised it. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 20 August 2026 an unmanned surface vessel, or sea drone, carrying explosives was detected a few hundred metres from the Neptun Deep offshore works, roughly 80 nautical miles east of Constanța in Romania’s exclusive economic zone. Whether it approached or drifted towards the works, and what it was intended to do, is unresolved.

A Romanian F-16 fired on it with its cannon, damaging but not fully destroying it, and a Navy explosive ordnance disposal team then neutralised it. Official reporting confirmed an explosive charge of unspecified size. The defence ministry initially described two drones and later corrected this to one. No casualties or damage to the infrastructure were reported.

The drone’s launch point and operator are unknown. Romania’s defence minister said Ukraine had confirmed it was not Ukrainian; that statement does not establish who did launch it. The case is separate from the aerial drone that crashed near Grindu the same day.

E048.headline: Navy destroys explosive drone debris found on Tuzla beach, Romania
E048.description: On 22 August 2026 the Navy destroyed explosive drone debris at Tuzla beach, Romania. It was preliminarily assessed as Ukrainian-made; operator unconfirmed.
summary: On 22 August 2026 fragments of an aerial drone containing explosives were found in the Tuzla beach area of Constanța County, Romania. The find was reported through the emergency services, the area was cordoned off, and specialists examined the object.

A preliminary assessment by the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (MApN) indicated Ukrainian manufacture. That finding is preliminary, and the drone’s operator and mission have not been confirmed. The date and route of its original flight are unknown, as is how many drones the fragments came from.

A Navy explosive ordnance disposal team carried out two controlled detonations because the first did not fully destroy the charge; both blasts were part of one disposal. Prosecutors at the Constanța Court of Appeal were notified. No casualties were reported.

E049.headline: Explosive Gerbera drone fragment neutralised off Gura Portiței, Romania
E049.description: On 23 August 2026 a floating Gerbera drone fragment containing explosives was neutralised at sea off Gura Portiței, Romania. Its operator is not established.
summary: On 23 August 2026 a suspect object was found floating in coastal waters off Gura Portiței, in Tulcea County, Romania. Navy explosive ordnance disposal specialists examined it; it was the body or a fragment of a Gerbera aerial drone containing explosive material.

The Romanian Ministry of National Defence confirmed the type and the explosive hazard. Earlier reporting called the drone Russian, and Gerbera is a type used by Russia, but the type alone does not establish who operated it. The date and route of its original flight are unknown, and the exact offshore jurisdiction was not specified.

The disposal team, working from a Coast Guard vessel, neutralised the object in place. No casualties were reported. The fragment came from an aerial drone, not a sea drone, and is not part of the Neptun Deep sea-drone incident.

E050.headline: Drone reported as Russian falls into tree near house in Ciușlea, Romania
E050.description: On 24 August 2026 a drone reported as Russian came down in a tree about 5 m from a home in Ciușlea, Vrancea County, Romania. It carried no explosives.
summary: On 24 August 2026 a drone came down in a tree about 5 metres from a house in Ciușlea, Vrancea County, Romania. It had reportedly entered Romanian airspace via Moldova.
The drone was reported as Russian; its precise model has not been established. The Romanian Ministry of National Defence (MApN) reported that it carried no explosive payload.

No injuries were reported despite how close the drone fell to the house. Fighter aircraft and a helicopter responded, the area was secured, and the drone was recovered for investigation. Earlier reporting also described a protective evacuation.

E051.headline: Suspected drone fragment found by Constanța Casino promenade, Romania
E051.description: On the evening of 25 August 2026 passers-by found a suspected drone fragment by the Constanța Casino promenade, Romania. Its origin has not been established.
summary: On the evening of 25 August 2026 passers-by noticed an object near the Constanța Casino in Romania. The object, a suspected drone component, had reportedly washed ashore between the breakwaters by the casino promenade. The find was reported in coverage on 26 August.
The object has not been confirmed as part of a drone, and its full identity, origin and operator have not been established. No explosives were identified when it was examined.
Firefighters and specialists recovered and examined the object, and no harm was reported. It is a separate find from the explosive drone found on Olimp beach the next morning.

E052.headline: Beach evacuated as explosive drone fragment detonated at Olimp, Romania
E052.description: On 26 August 2026 Olimp beach in Constanța County, Romania, was evacuated and an explosive drone fragment found there was detonated. No origin was announced.
summary: On 26 August 2026 a drone fragment containing explosive material was found on the tourist beach at Olimp, Constanța County, Romania. The beach was evacuated, access was restricted, a cordon was set up, and an RO-Alert warning was issued.
Specialists from the SRI Antiterrorist Brigade detonated the material on the beach in a controlled explosion. No casualties were reported.
The authorities had not announced the fragment’s origin or the drone model in reporting from 26–27 August, and the date and route of the original flight are unknown.

E053.headline: Merchant ship Progress IV sinks off Romania; drone strike unconfirmed
E053.description: On 27 August 2026 the ship Progress IV caught fire and sank off Sfântu Gheorghe in Romania’s EEZ. All 12 crew were rescued; a drone strike is unconfirmed.
summary: On 27 August 2026 the merchant vessel Progress IV caught fire and sank in the Black Sea, about 15–20 nautical miles off Sfântu Gheorghe in Romania’s exclusive economic zone. A distress call came around 17:55 local time, and all 12 crew members had been rescued by 20:47.

An impact on the ship was alleged, and the authorities said its cause required investigation. A drone attack remained a hypothesis: no drone or other weapon has been identified, and no explosion or drone strike has been established. The ship’s flag was reported as the Dominican Republic, while a shipping-industry source cited Dominica.

One crew member was injured, reportedly with a fractured arm; earlier descriptions of a serious injury are not supported by later accounts. The maritime rescue coordination centre (MRCC) coordinated a commercial vessel, the Border Police and rescue ships.

E054.headline: Shepherd finds explosive drone near Viișoara, Romania; origin disputed
E054.description: On 1 September 2026 a shepherd found a damaged drone with explosives in a field near Viișoara, Vaslui County, Romania. Its official origin is unresolved.
summary: On 1 September 2026 a shepherd tending sheep found a damaged drone (UAV) in a field near Viișoara, Vaslui County, in Romania. The date is the verified discovery date, not an established crash date: the finder did not see the drone fall, and its flight route and crash time are unknown. Before the authorities arrived, the shepherd handled the drone and disconnected some of its parts.

Specialists confirmed that it contained explosive material. The type of drone has not been confirmed, and its official origin is unresolved: local reports offered conflicting claims that it was Russian or Ukrainian, and the device's identity and provenance were under investigation.
Gendarmes secured the site and SRI bomb specialists destroyed the drone in a controlled detonation. Prosecutors at the Iași Court of Appeal were notified. No casualties were reported.

E055.headline: Mapping drone of unknown origin recovered on Finland's southern coast
E055.description: On 2 September 2026 a mapping drone of unknown origin was recovered on the southern Finnish coast. A possible territorial violation was investigated.
summary: On 2 September 2026 authorities recovered a survey or mapping drone (UAV) on the southern coast of Finland. The precise location was not given in the cited report. The date is the recovery date; when the drone flew, and along which route, is unknown.
The drone's origin and operator are unknown. It has not been established that it came from abroad, and it is not assumed to be a foreign military drone.

The drone was described as non-dangerous, with no hazardous payload identified, and no damage or casualties were reported. Authorities investigated whether the flight amounted to a territorial violation.

E056.headline: Reported Russian jet drone crosses into northeastern Romania from Moldova
E056.description: On 8 September 2026 a jet drone reported as Russian flew from Moldova into northeastern Romania for about 30 minutes, prompting Iași Airport restrictions.
summary: On 8 September 2026 a jet-powered drone entered Romanian airspace from Moldova at about 16:37 local time and crossed the Neamț, Botoșani and Iași sector of northeastern Romania. It stayed in Romanian airspace for roughly 30 minutes before leaving for Moldova, where it reportedly crashed. Timings for individual parts of the flight vary between accounts.
The drone was reported as Russian. Its technical identification as a jet-powered Geran-4 is attributed to Romanian and Moldovan reporting.

Two Spanish F/A-18 fighters were scrambled, and authorities monitored the flight and warned residents. Restrictions were imposed at Iași Airport and civil alerts were issued. No impact or casualties were reported in Romania; the reported crash happened outside the EU, in Moldova.

E057.headline: Suspected Russian military drone recovered off Rusinowo beach, Poland
E057.description: On 14 September 2026 Poland’s military pulled a drone from the sea off Rusinowo beach; the defence minister’s preliminary assessment is that it is Russian.
summary: On 14 September 2026 the Polish military located a suspected military drone in the Baltic Sea just off Rusinowo beach, close to Jarosławiec on the coast of Poland, and pulled it from the water for examination. The date is that of the discovery and recovery; when the drone flew, and by what route it reached the Polish coast, is not known.

Poland’s defence minister said the preliminary assessment was that it was a Russian military drone. That identification is preliminary and depends on the examination of the recovered drone. No payload was reported.
No casualties or damage were reported in connection with the find.

E058.headline: Italian NATO fighter shoots down Gerbera drone near Pratkūnai, Lithuania
E058.description: Overnight on 14–15 September 2026 an Italian NATO jet shot down a Gerbera drone, a type used by Russia, near Pratkūnai, Lithuania. No casualties were reported.
summary: Overnight on 14–15 September 2026 an Italian fighter jet operating with NATO engaged and shot down a drone over Lithuania near Pratkūnai. Lithuanian authorities then examined the debris and the drone’s electronics. No casualties were reported.

The drone was identified as a Gerbera, a type used by Russia. On 16 September Lithuania’s president assessed that it had likely been intended for a Ukrainian target. A possible diversion by Ukrainian electronic warfare has been put forward to explain how it reached Lithuania, but that causal account is an assessment. Neither the Russian-type identification nor the intended-target assessment is proof of a deliberate attack on Lithuania.
Whether this particular drone carried explosives was not established; Gerbera variants may be decoys or armed.

E059.headline: Romania says Russian drone’s payload detonated mid-air before Solca crash
E059.description: On 24 September 2026 a drone that entered from Ukraine crashed near Solca, Romania, after its payload detonated mid-air. Romanian officials called it Russian.
summary: On 24 September 2026 a small drone crossed from Ukraine into Romanian airspace over northern Botoșani and crashed in woodland near Solca, in Suceava County, after about four minutes in Romanian airspace; military radar confirmed the entry. Minister Miruță said its explosive load separated shortly before the crash and detonated in the air. Residents located and filmed the wreckage.

Miruță described a Russian-model drone with equipment Romanian specialists had not encountered before. The Institute for the Study of War identified the wreckage from geolocated imagery as a Russian Gerbera-type drone; that is ISW’s assessment, not an official Romanian model identification. Lithuania’s Foreign Ministry attributed the wider 24 September incursions into Romania and Moldova to Russian drones. The launching unit, intended target and cause of the incursion remain unresolved.

Two Romanian F-16s took off from Borcea to monitor the drone, and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter launched from Bacău at 07:21. Miruță said the conditions for engaging it were not met; it was not shot down. Interior Ministry teams secured the site. No casualties or material damage were reported, and there was no fire at the crash site.

E060.headline: Drone of unknown origin flies along Chilia branch in Romania
E060.description: On the night of 12–13 August 2026 a drone flew about 10 minutes along the Chilia branch in Romania before leaving for Ukraine. Its origin is not established.
summary: On the night of 12–13 August 2026 a drone (UAV) entered Romanian airspace and flew for about 10 minutes along the Chilia branch, then left towards Ukraine, exiting around 13 km southwest of Chilia Veche. The Romanian military monitored the flight. Explosions were reported after the drone left, but no impact in Romania has been established.
The drone's nationality and operator have not been established, and its identity remains unresolved.

Romanian F-16s also responded to a later target nearby. The overnight track was reported alongside the discovery of drone fragments at Costinești beach the same day, but the two have not been linked, and the drone's relationship to later recoveries is unresolved.

E061.headline: Drone fragments of unknown origin found on Costinești beach, Romania
E061.description: On 13 and 14 August 2026 aerial-drone fragments were found at Tineretului beach in Costinești, Romania. Their origin and the number of drones are unknown.
summary: At around 08:15 on 13 August 2026, aerial-drone material was reported near the breakwaters of Tineretului beach in Costinești, Romania, after drifting ashore. Tourist access was restricted. Another fragment was found nearby the next day, 14 August.

The origin and operator of the material have not been established. Officials identified it as fragments of an aerial drone, not a maritime drone. How the fragments relate to each other, how many separate drones they came from and their exact provenance were under investigation, and no flight route was observed.

Military divers and explosive-ordnance disposal specialists, the Coast Guard and other emergency services responded and recovered the material. No pyrotechnic risk was reported for the material examined, and no injuries were reported. Appeals prosecutors in Constanța were notified.

E062.headline: Drone fragment of unknown origin washes ashore at Saturn beach, Romania
E062.description: On 14 August 2026 waves carried an aerial-drone fragment onto Saturn beach in Constanța County, Romania. Tourists alerted authorities; its origin is unresolved.
summary: On the afternoon of 14 August 2026 waves carried a fragment of an aerial drone onto Saturn beach in Constanța County, on the Romanian coast. Tourists alerted the authorities, and access to the area was restricted while the object was examined.

Who launched the drone, and what type of drone the fragment came from, has not been established. Romanian reporting on the find also covered fragments found at Costinești, but no link between the two finds has been established.
Specialists reported that the fragment contained no pyrotechnic elements. It was examined and recovered, and no injuries were reported.

E063.headline: Drone crashes in northern Tulcea, Romania; wreckage in Măcin Mountains
E063.description: On 14 August 2026 at least one drone crashed in northern Tulcea County, Romania, with wreckage later reported in the Măcin Mountains. Its origin is unknown.
summary: On 14 August 2026 at least one drone crashed in northern Tulcea County, Romania. An emergency call reported a crash in a forest, which caused localised burning. Initial reports placed it near Luncavița and Cetățuia; later reports located wreckage near Greci, in the Măcin Mountains. The drone reportedly flew low enough to escape radar, and its route is unknown.
The drone’s origin and model were not established in contemporary reporting. It is also unresolved whether the Luncavița and Greci reports describe one crash site or linked or separate sites.

Military specialists responded with helicopter support, and the Border Police set up a cordon. A later follow-up reported a controlled disposal in the Măcin Mountains the same day; the exact charge was not established. No casualties or property damage were reported. A separate object discovered the same day at Plauru is a different incident.

E064.headline: Drone found near Plauru, Romania, destroyed by specialists next day
E064.description: A drone found near Plauru, Tulcea County, Romania, on 14 August 2026 was destroyed in a controlled detonation on 15 August. Its origin and model are unknown.
summary: On 14 August 2026 a Romanian military team identified a drone near Plauru, in Tulcea County near the Ukrainian border. The site was secured the same day, and on 15 August specialists destroyed the object in a controlled detonation.

The drone’s nationality and model have not been established, and the releases from the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (MApN) gave no technical details. The date and route of its original flight are unknown: 14 August is when it was discovered, not necessarily when it flew.
No casualties were reported, and the exact payload was not specified. The Plauru find was at a different location from the wreckage reported in the Măcin Mountains the same day.

E065.headline: Starter motor found off Tyulenovo, Bulgaria; drone link not established
E065.description: On 14 August 2026 the Bulgarian Navy recovered an object drifting about 50 m off Tyulenovo, Bulgaria, identified as a starter motor. Any drone link is unproven.
summary: On 14 August 2026 the Bulgarian Navy examined an object drifting about 50 metres offshore at Tyulenovo, in Bulgaria’s Dobrich district, and took it to a naval base.

The object was identified only as a starter motor. It has not been established that it came from a drone, so it is not a confirmed drone find, and its origin is unknown. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this object. When and how it ended up in the sea is also unknown.
No casualties were reported.

E066.headline: Reconnaissance drone of unknown origin washes ashore at Primorsko, Bulgaria
E066.description: On 14 August 2026 a reconnaissance drone washed ashore on Primorsko beach, Burgas district, Bulgaria, and the Navy took it to base. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 14 August 2026 a reconnaissance drone (UAV) washed ashore on the beach at Primorsko, in Bulgaria’s Burgas district. It was examined, and the Bulgarian Navy transported it to a naval base.

No operator has been identified for the drone, and the release reporting the find gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When it came down and what route it flew are unknown.
No casualties were reported, and any payload was not specified.

E067.headline: Drone parts of unknown origin found on Lozenets beach, Bulgaria
E067.description: On 14 August 2026 drone parts were found on Lozenets beach in the Burgas district of Bulgaria and recovered by the Navy. Who operated the drone is unresolved.
summary: On 14 August 2026 drone parts were discovered on the beach at Lozenets, in Bulgaria’s Burgas district. The find prompted a response from the Bulgarian Navy, which recovered the parts to a base.

No operator has been identified, and the release reporting the find gave no final identification of the drone. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify these parts. The date the drone came down and its original route are unknown.
No casualties were reported, and any payload was not specified.

E068.headline: Unverified report of aircraft or drone debris near Albena, Bulgaria
E068.description: A secondary report says aircraft or drone debris was recovered on the coast between Albena and Kranevo, Bulgaria, on 22 August 2026. It is unverified.
summary: A secondary report says that on 22 August 2026 debris described as coming from an aircraft or drone was found on the coast between the Albena resort and Kranevo in Bulgaria, prompting a naval response. The debris was reportedly inspected and recovered.

The account comes only from a secondary SofiaBeacon report that recalled two coastal debris recoveries on 22 August. The exact object, its origin and the original official release have not been verified. No operator has been identified, and associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this debris. When and how it reached the coast is unknown.
No casualties were reported.

E069.headline: Unverified report of aircraft or drone debris at Rakitnika, Bulgaria
E069.description: A secondary report says aircraft or drone debris was recovered in the Rakitnika area near Varna, Bulgaria, on 22 August 2026. The account is unverified.
summary: A secondary report says that on 22 August 2026 debris described as coming from an aircraft or drone was found in the Rakitnika area near Varna, Bulgaria. The Navy reportedly inspected and recovered it.

The account comes only from a secondary SofiaBeacon report that recalled two coastal debris recoveries on 22 August and identified Rakitnika as a response site. The exact object, its origin and the original official release have not been verified. No operator has been identified, and associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this debris.
No casualties were reported.

E070.headline: Electric reconnaissance drone recovered at sea near Tsarevo, Bulgaria
E070.description: On 25 August 2026 the Bulgarian Navy recovered an electric reconnaissance drone from the sea between Tsarevo and Varvara, Bulgaria. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 25 August 2026 an electric reconnaissance drone (UAV) was found in the sea between Tsarevo and Varvara, Bulgaria. It was inspected at sea and reported to be non-dangerous, and a Bulgarian Navy team from Burgas transported it to base.

No operator has been identified for the drone, and the releases reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When the drone came down and the route it flew are unknown.
No casualties were reported.

E071.headline: Military drone wing washes ashore on Kamchia coast, Bulgaria
E071.description: On the evening of 25 August 2026 a military-drone wing washed ashore on the Kamchia resort coast, Bulgaria, and the Navy recovered it. Origin unresolved.
summary: On the evening of 25 August 2026 a wing from a military drone washed ashore on the coast at the Kamchia resort in Bulgaria. A Bulgarian Navy team from Varna recovered it.

The wing carried no ammunition. No operator has been identified, and the releases reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this wing. When and where the drone came down is unknown.
No casualties were reported. It has not been established whether the wing belongs to the same aircraft as a drone reported in a separate response on 27 August.

E072.headline: Drone remains recovered from Kabakum beach near Varna, Bulgaria
E072.description: On 26 August 2026 drone remains found on Kabakum beach near Varna, Bulgaria, were taken to Varna by the Navy. No explosives were found; origin is unresolved.
summary: Early on 26 August 2026, after an alert received at about 01:30, Kabakum beach (also spelled Cabacum) near Varna, Bulgaria, was secured following the discovery of drone remains. Reports described the material both as a UAV and as fuselage remains.
The Bulgarian Navy inspected the material, found no explosives, and transported it to Varna.

No operator has been identified, and the releases gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When the drone came down is unknown. No casualties were reported.

E073.headline: Floating drone destroyed at sea by Navy near Pomorie, Bulgaria
E073.description: On 26 August 2026 the Navy destroyed a floating drone at sea near Pomorie, Bulgaria. The exact charge was not stated, and the drone’s origin is unresolved.
summary: On 26 August 2026 a floating object in the Black Sea near Pomorie, Bulgaria, was identified as a drone (UAV). The Bulgarian Navy destroyed it at sea.

The exact charge was not stated, and the controlled destruction does not by itself show that the drone carried a live warhead. No operator has been identified, and the releases reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When the drone came down and the route it flew are unknown.
No casualties were reported.

E074.headline: Drone destroyed at sea by Navy at Pasha Dere, south of Varna, Bulgaria
E074.description: On 26 August 2026 the Navy destroyed a drone at sea at Pasha Dere, south of Varna, Bulgaria. The exact charge was not stated; its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 26 August 2026 a drone (UAV) was inspected in coastal waters at Pasha Dere, south of Varna, Bulgaria. The Bulgarian Navy destroyed it at sea.

The exact charge was not stated, and the controlled destruction does not in itself establish that the drone carried an explosive payload. No operator has been identified, and the releases reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When the drone came down and the route it flew are unknown.
No casualties were reported.

E075.headline: Part-submerged drone towed to Varna from sea off Cape Galata, Bulgaria
E075.description: On 26 August 2026 a part-submerged drone found 2.6 nautical miles northeast of Cape Galata, Bulgaria, was towed to Varna Naval Base. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 26 August 2026 a part-submerged aerial drone (UAV) was found in the sea 2.6 nautical miles northeast of Cape Galata, Bulgaria. Its engine and nose were under water, with the tail visible.
No explosive material was found. The drone was towed to Varna Naval Base and lifted out of the water.

No operator has been identified, and the release reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this one. When the drone came down and the route it flew are unknown. No casualties were reported.

E076.headline: Drone wing found by Laguna campground at Golden Sands, Bulgaria
E076.description: On 26 August 2026 a drone wing was found near the beach at the Laguna campground in Golden Sands resort, Bulgaria, and taken by the Navy. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 26 August 2026 a drone wing was found near the resort beach at the Laguna campground in Golden Sands, Bulgaria. A Bulgarian Navy team from Varna transported it to base.

No operator has been identified, and the release reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this wing. Any payload was not specified, and when the drone came down is unknown. No casualties were reported.

E077.headline: Drone wing recovered from northern beach of Burgas, Bulgaria
E077.description: On 26 August 2026 the Navy recovered a drone wing from the northern beach of Burgas, Bulgaria; it was first reported as a UAV. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 26 August 2026 an object on the northern beach of Burgas, Bulgaria, was first reported as a drone (UAV) and then found to be a drone wing. A Bulgarian Navy team from Burgas recovered it.

No operator has been identified, and the release reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this wing. Any payload was not specified, and when the drone came down is unknown. No casualties were reported.

E078.headline: Floating drone tail section recovered south of Kavarna, Bulgaria
E078.description: On 27 August 2026 a Bulgarian naval team recovered a floating drone tail section 8 nautical miles south of Kavarna, Bulgaria. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On 27 August 2026 a Bulgarian naval team identified a floating drone fragment, the tail section, in the sea 8 nautical miles south of Kavarna, Bulgaria. It was transported to Varna Naval Base.

No operator has been identified, and the release reporting it gave no final identification. Associations with Russian or Ukrainian drones made for the wider group of finds do not identify this tail section. When the drone came down and the route it flew are unknown.
Any payload was not specified, and no casualties were reported.

E079.headline: Drone with no explosives recovered from Black Sea at Kamchia, Bulgaria
E079.description: On 27 August 2026 a drone with no explosives on board was found in Black Sea waters at Kamchia, Bulgaria, and taken to Varna Naval Base. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 27 August 2026 a team inspected an object reported in Black Sea waters at Kamchia, on Bulgaria's coast, and identified it as a drone (UAV). The date is the discovery and response date: when the drone came down, and the route it flew, are unknown.

The origin of this drone has not been established, and no operator has been identified. Broader Russian or Ukrainian associations made for this group of coastal finds do not identify this particular object.

No explosives were on board and no casualties were reported. The drone was transported to Varna Naval Base. Its relationship to a drone wing reported on 25 August is unresolved; the two are not assumed to be the same object.

E080.headline: Suspected drone seen off Chernomorets, Bulgaria; debris found on beach
E080.description: On 27 August 2026 a suspected drone was seen about 1–1.5 km off Chernomorets, Bulgaria; beach debris was reported recovered on 28 August. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 27 August 2026 an object suspected to be a drone (UAV) was seen about 1–1.5 km offshore from Chernomorets, in Sozopol municipality on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. A report on 28 August said drone debris had been recovered from the beach there.

The origin of the drone has not been established and no operator has been identified. Broader Russian or Ukrainian associations made for this group of coastal finds do not identify this particular object. It has also not been proven that the beach debris came from the object seen offshore.
No casualties were reported. The Navy in Burgas responded and transported the debris to base. When the drone came down, and the route it flew, are unknown.

E081.headline: Navy destroys drone spotted near Sveti Ivan island at Sozopol, Bulgaria
E081.description: A drone spotted on 27 August 2026 at the northern pier opposite Sveti Ivan island, Sozopol, Bulgaria, was destroyed in place by the Navy. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 27 August 2026 a drone (UAV) was spotted at the northern pier opposite Sveti Ivan island, in the Sozopol area on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The Bulgarian Navy destroyed the object in place, in a controlled disposal announced on 28 August; the exact time of the disposal was not specified.

The origin of this drone has not been established, and no operator has been identified. Broader Russian or Ukrainian associations made for this group of coastal finds do not identify this particular object. When it came down, and the route it flew, are unknown.
The exact hazard posed by the object was not specified, and no casualties were reported. The destruction was a controlled disposal by the authorities, not an explosion caused by the drone itself.

E082.headline: Naval team recovers drone 1 km north of Shabla Lighthouse, Bulgaria
E082.description: On 28 August 2026 a naval team found a drone about 1 km north of Shabla Lighthouse, Bulgaria, assessed it as safe and took it to Varna. Origin unresolved.
summary: On 28 August 2026 a naval team found and identified a drone (UAV) about 1 km north of Shabla Lighthouse on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The date is the discovery and response date: when the drone came down, and the route it flew, are unknown.

The origin of this drone has not been established and no operator has been identified. Broader Russian or Ukrainian associations made for this group of coastal finds do not identify this particular object.

The drone was assessed as safe and transported to the naval base at Varna. No casualties were reported. Although Shabla is a separate recovery site, it has not been established that this is a different drone from those found elsewhere on the coast.

E083.headline: Navy identifies drone debris on Bungalata beach at Ahtopol, Bulgaria
E083.description: On 28 August 2026 the Bulgarian Navy identified drone debris on Bungalata beach in Ahtopol, Bulgaria, and took it to base. Its origin has not been established.
summary: On 28 August 2026 the Bulgarian Navy identified material found on Bungalata beach in Ahtopol, on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, as debris from a drone (UAV). The date is the discovery and response date: when the drone came down, and the route it flew, are unknown.

The origin of the debris has not been established and no operator has been identified. Broader Russian or Ukrainian associations made for this group of coastal finds do not identify this particular object.

No casualties were reported. A Navy team from Burgas transported the material to base. Although Bungalata beach is a separate recovery site, it has not been established that the debris comes from a different drone than other finds on the coast.

E084.headline: Unidentified aerial target north of Snake Island prompts alert near Romania
E084.description: On 27 August 2026 two Spanish F-18s scrambled after an unidentified aerial target 33 km north of Snake Island. No entry into Romanian airspace was established.
summary: On 27 August 2026 an aerial target was reported over the Black Sea 33 km north of Snake Island, near the Ukrainian Black Sea sector. It was detected on radar, and two Spanish F-18 fighters were scrambled in a NATO response on the Romanian side. The exact time has not been established.

The target's full identity as a drone (UAV) has not been established, and its origin is unknown. It was reported outside demonstrated Romanian airspace and no entry into Romania was established, so the alert is not a confirmed incursion into the EU.
