No impact in Romania was established. The alert was reported alongside coverage of a maritime incident involving the Progress IV, whose impact mechanism is unknown, but no causal link between the two has been shown. The alert is not evidence of what caused the Progress IV incident.

N004.headline: Lithuanian border guards force down cigarette smuggling drone near Purvėnai
N004.description: On the night of 27 January 2026 border guards forced down a cargo drone carrying cigarettes near Purvėnai, Lithuania, in a smuggling case linked to Belarus.
summary: On the night of 27 January 2026, Lithuania’s State Border Guard Service (VSAT) detected a quadcopter entering Lithuania near the village of Purvėnai in the Šalčininkai district. The official release, issued on 28 January, referred to Tuesday night without saying on which side of midnight the flight took place. After an electronic counter-drone intervention the drone was forced down, and border guards recovered it together with nearby cargo of 1,000 packs of Belarus-stamped cigarettes.

The drone was reported to have approached from Belarus, and VSAT attributed the flight to smugglers operating across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. The case was handled as a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike, and it is not evidence of an attack by a foreign state.
No casualties or damage to third parties were reported. The drone and the cigarette cargo were seized.

N005.headline: Cigarette smuggling drone retrieved from pine tree near Milvydai, Lithuania
N005.description: On the night of 23–24 February 2026 a cigarette smuggling drone was intercepted near Milvydai, Lithuania, and later retrieved from a pine tree near the border.
summary: On the night of 23–24 February 2026, Lithuanian border guards intercepted a cargo drone near Milvydai in the Šalčininkai district, close to the border with Belarus. After an electronic counter-drone intervention, the drone ended up lodged in the crown of a pine tree about 0.5 km from the border. It was carrying 500 packs of cigarettes. On 24 February forestry staff helped the border guards retrieve it, and the State Border Guard Service (VSAT) published the case on 25 February.

VSAT attributed the flight to smugglers operating across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established, and the drone’s full flight track was not made public. The case was treated as a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike, and is not evidence of an attack by a foreign state.
No casualties or third-party damage were reported. The drone and its cargo were seized, and administrative proceedings followed.

N010.headline: Cigarette smuggling drone from Belarus brought down near Dubas, Lithuania
N010.description: On the night of 5 April 2026 Lithuanian border guards brought down a drone smuggling cigarettes from Belarus near Dubas, in the Varėna district.
summary: On the night of 5 April 2026, possibly continuing into 6 April, Lithuanian border guards used thermal surveillance to detect an inbound drone near the village of Dubas in the Varėna district. Counter-drone action brought it down in nearby woodland. The drone was carrying 1,000 packs of NZ Gold cigarettes.

The drone was reported to have approached from Belarus, and the State Border Guard Service (VSAT) attributed the flight to smugglers operating across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. The case was a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike, and is not evidence of an attack by a foreign state.
No casualties or third-party damage were reported. The drone and its cargo were seized and administrative proceedings followed. VSAT published the case on 7 April 2026.

N011.headline: Smuggling drone crashes near Krupaviesai, Lithuania, after interception
N011.description: Before dawn on 7 May 2026 a cargo drone carrying cigarettes crashed into a field near Krupaviesai, Lithuania, after counter-drone action by border guards.
summary: Before dawn on 7 May 2026 Lithuanian border guards used counter-drone measures against a loaded cargo drone near Krupaviesai in the Šalčininkai district. The intervention brought the drone down into a field, and it was broken. It was carrying 850 packs of Minsk Capital QS cigarettes.

The drone was reported to have approached from Belarus, and the State Border Guard Service (VSAT) attributed the flight to smugglers operating across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. The flight was a criminal cargo operation, not a military strike, and is not evidence of an attack by a foreign state.
No casualties or third-party damage were reported. The broken drone and its cargo were seized. VSAT, which published the case on 8 May, described it as the year’s 17th such interception.

N012.headline: Border guards force down cigarette-laden drone in Šalčininkai, Lithuania
N012.description: On 14 June 2026 Lithuanian border guards forced down a cigarette-smuggling drone reported approaching from Belarus in Šalčininkai district, Lithuania.
summary: On Sunday 14 June 2026 Lithuanian border guards detected a homemade cargo drone approaching near Daugidonys, in Šalčininkai district on the Belarus border, and used counter-drone equipment against it. The drone came down and was recovered in fields at Dimitrai. It was carrying 200 packs of NZ Gold cigarettes. The incident was reported on Monday 15 June.

According to Lithuania's border guard service (VSAT), the drone was flown by smugglers operating from or across the Belarus border. The operator's nationality has not been established, and nor has any state sponsorship; the official account describes a criminal cargo operation, not a military strike, and is not evidence of a foreign-state attack.

No casualties or third-party damage were reported. The drone was brought down by electronic means, recovered and seized, and administrative proceedings followed. It is not classified as a shoot-down or a confirmed crash.

N015.headline: Germany arrests Moldovan over suspected drone espionage in Munich
N015.description: On 15 July 2026 a man was arrested in Munich, Germany, after a drone filmed a defence manufacturer's site. Investigators allege espionage; no state is named.
summary: On the evening of Wednesday 15 July 2026, residents in Munich, Germany, alerted police to a drone filming the premises of a weapons manufacturer. A Reuters security source named the company as KNDS. A 37-year-old Moldovan suspect was arrested near the site, and an arrest warrant and remand were announced on Friday 17 July.

Investigators alleged that he was gathering intelligence for a foreign entity or prohibited organisation, but no sponsoring state has been named. The drone is alleged to have been launched locally; no cross-border flight is alleged. The suspect's citizenship alone does not show direction by a foreign state, and the case is an allegation, not a conviction.
The drone's model was not specified, and no payload or damage was reported.

N023.headline: Greek reports: F-16s intercepted Turkish UAV between Samothrace and Lemnos
N023.description: On 28 August 2026 Greek reports said F-16s intercepted a Turkish military UAV between Samothrace and Lemnos, Greece. Attribution rests on the Greek account.
summary: On the morning of 28 August 2026 a drone (UAV) was reported flying in the northern Aegean between Samothrace and Lemnos and near the Alexandroupoli airport area. According to Greek reporting, two Greek F-16 fighters identified or intercepted it. No firing or shoot-down was reported, and the exact track has not been published.

Greek reporting described the UAV as a Turkish military drone and the flight as an airspace violation. Both characterisations come from the Greek account; they have not been independently adjudicated, and no independent forensic attribution has been claimed. The model and the exact number of crossings were not specified.

The Greek account links the encounter to a precaution taken by an Aegean passenger flight near Alexandroupoli airport, which reportedly followed an alternative path or a low-altitude precaution before continuing to Athens. No collision or casualties were reported. The airport precaution is treated as part of the same encounter, not as a separate incident.

N028.headline: Navy destroys floating drone at sea off Pomorie Reef, Bulgaria
N028.description: On 2 September 2026 the Bulgarian Navy destroyed a floating drone about 9 nautical miles off Burgas bridge and Pomorie Reef. Its operator is unknown.
summary: On 2 September 2026 a floating drone (UAV) was found about 9 nautical miles opposite the Burgas bridge and Pomorie Reef, in what were reported as Bulgarian coastal or territorial waters. Navy personnel identified it and destroyed it at sea. The operation was announced on 3 September.

No operator or national origin has been announced for this object, and its model was not specified. When it flew or came down, and whether it is linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are unresolved. No payload was reported, and none can be inferred from the way it was destroyed.
The site was one of three offshore responses handled from the Navy's Burgas base in an official announcement covering six Navy tasks. It is separate from an earlier find at Pomorie on 26 August.

N029.headline: Reconnaissance drone found on Cape Kaliakra seashore in Bulgaria
N029.description: On 2 September 2026 Bulgarian naval personnel identified a find on the Cape Kaliakra seashore as a reconnaissance drone. Its operator and origin are unresolved.
summary: On 2 September 2026 naval personnel identified an object found on the seashore at Cape Kaliakra, on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, as a reconnaissance drone (UAV). The find was announced on 3 September.

The drone's model, operator and manufacturer have not been announced, and its origin is unresolved. When it flew or came down, and whether it is linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are not known. No payload was reported.
The drone was transported to Varna Naval Base. This shoreline recovery is separate from an offshore operation on 6 September.

N030.headline: Navy destroys floating drone at sea off Cape Kolokita, Bulgaria
N030.description: On 2 September 2026 the Bulgarian Navy identified a floating drone in waters off Cape Kolokita, Bulgaria, and destroyed it at sea. Its operator is unknown.
summary: On 2 September 2026 a drone (UAV) was found floating in the waters off Cape Kolokita, reported as Bulgarian coastal or territorial waters. The Navy identified it and destroyed it at sea. The response was announced on 3 September.

No operator or national origin has been announced, and the model was not specified. The date of the drone's flight or crash is unknown, as is any link to other airframes recovered on the Bulgarian coast. No payload was reported, and the method of destruction is not evidence of one.
Cape Kolokita was identified as a separate location in the same official release, which described six Navy tasks; it was one of three offshore response sites handled from the Navy's Burgas base.

N031.headline: Navy destroys floating drone material at sea off Maslen Nos, Bulgaria
N031.description: On 2 September 2026 the Bulgarian Navy identified floating drone material in waters off Maslen Nos, Bulgaria, and destroyed it at sea. Its operator is unknown.
summary: On 2 September 2026 floating material in the waters off Maslen Nos, reported as Bulgarian coastal or territorial waters, was identified by the Navy as coming from a drone (UAV). Navy personnel destroyed the material at sea. The operation was announced on 3 September.

No operator or national origin has been announced, and the drone's model was not specified. It is not known when the drone flew or came down, or whether the material is linked to other drones recovered along the coast. No payload was reported, and none should be inferred from the disposal method.
Maslen Nos was listed as a distinct location in an official announcement of six Navy tasks, as one of three offshore sites handled from the Navy's Burgas base.

N032.headline: Military drone fragments found on Pomorie town beach in Bulgaria
N032.description: On 2 September 2026 Navy personnel from Burgas responded to unidentified military-drone fragments on Pomorie town beach, Bulgaria. Operator unknown.
summary: On 2 September 2026 Navy personnel from Burgas responded to military-drone fragments found on the town beach in Pomorie, on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The find was announced on 3 September.

The fragments were officially reported as military-drone debris, but the drone has not been identified: its operator is unknown, and the number of aircraft involved is not known. When the aircraft flew or came down, and whether the fragments are linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are unresolved. No payload was reported.
A naval examination was reported, but the final method of handling the fragments was not specified. This beach find is separate from an offshore find on 26 August.

N033.headline: Cone-shaped object on Topola beach in Bulgaria not confirmed as a drone
N033.description: On 2 September 2026 a cone-shaped object found on Topola beach, Dobrich, Bulgaria, was taken to Varna Naval Base. It has not been confirmed as a drone.
summary: On 2 September 2026 a suspicious cone-shaped object was found on Topola beach, in Dobrich, Bulgaria. It was included in an official announcement of six Navy tasks, published on 3 September, and was taken to Varna Naval Base.

The object's identity has not been established, and it has not been confirmed as a drone (UAV); its shape alone does not show that it is one. Its origin is unknown, and a foreign origin has not been shown. No route or payload was reported.
The Topola find is separate from an earlier find recorded at Tyulenovo on 14 August.

N035.headline: Navy retrieves drone found afloat off Cape Kaliakra in Bulgaria
N035.description: In the late afternoon of 6 September 2026 the Navy retrieved a floating drone about 650 m northeast of Cape Kaliakra, Bulgaria. Its origin was not announced.
summary: In the late afternoon of 6 September 2026 a Navy team from Varna retrieved a floating drone (UAV) from coastal waters about 3.5 cables, or 650 m, northeast of Cape Kaliakra on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The team was activated at the request of the Interior Ministry. The operation was reported on 7 September.
The drone's type, origin and operator have not been announced. When it flew or came down, and whether it is linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are unresolved.
The drone was assessed as safe for retrieval, although no detailed payload information was published, and it was taken to the naval base.

N036.headline: Lithuanian border guards seize cigarette smuggling drone at Daugidonys
N036.description: On 6 September 2026 border guards intercepted a homemade drone carrying cigarettes into Lithuania at Daugidonys, Šalčininkai; VSAT said it came from Belarus.
summary: Just after midnight on 6 September 2026, during the night of 5–6 September, Lithuanian border guards (VSAT) intercepted a homemade cargo drone (UAV) at Daugidonys in the Šalčininkai district, on Lithuania's border. The drone was carrying 1,000 packs of cigarettes. VSAT reported the operation on 7 September.

According to VSAT, the drone was flown by smugglers operating across the border from Belarus. The operators' nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. This was a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike, and the official account is a border-enforcement one, not evidence of a foreign-state attack.

The guards stopped the drone electronically, forcing it to descend; this is not classified as a shoot-down or a confirmed crash. The drone and its cargo were seized, and no casualties or damage to others were reported. VSAT described it as the year's 55th such case. It is separate from an earlier incident recorded at Daugidonys.

N038.headline: Drone fragments found on Capu Midia beach, Romania, neutralised by Navy
N038.description: Drone fragments reported on Capu Midia beach, Romania, on the evening of 9 September 2026 were neutralised by Navy EOD the next morning. Origin unresolved.
summary: At about 20:00 on 9 September 2026 aerial-drone fragments were reported on Capu Midia beach in Constanța County, on Romania's Black Sea coast. The area was isolated overnight, and a Navy explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team responded at about 09:30 on 10 September and neutralised the material. The two dates are stages of one incident.

The Defence Ministry (MApN) reported that the fragments carried no explosive charge. No operator or national origin has been confirmed, the number of drones the fragments came from was not specified, and the original flight is unknown.

The neutralisation was a controlled disposal by the authorities, not an explosion during the incident. Separate finds notified to police at Mamaia Nord and Corbu on 10 September are distinct from this one.

N040.headline: Tourists find damaged military-type drone on Kavatsi beach in Bulgaria
N040.description: On 11 September 2026 tourists found a damaged military-type drone on Kavatsi beach near Sozopol, Bulgaria. Its operator and national origin are unconfirmed.
summary: On 11 September 2026 tourists found a drone washed up on the Kavatsi tourist beach near Sozopol, on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. The drone body was damaged and its model was not specified. Specialists were summoned and the area was secured.

Reports described the drone as military in appearance, but that is not a confirmed national or operator attribution, and no final assessment has been reported. When it flew or came down, and whether it is linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are unresolved.
The final disposal outcome was not established in the report available. The Kavatsi find is separate from a late-August find at the Sveti Ivan pier in the Sozopol area.

N042.headline: Aerial drone debris recovered 46 nautical miles east of Midia, Romania
N042.description: On 11 September 2026 two drone fragments were recovered about 46 nautical miles east of Midia, outside Romania's territorial sea. Origin unknown.
summary: On 11 September 2026 a merchant ship reported two aerial-drone fragments in the Black Sea about 46 nautical miles east of Midia, Romania. A Coast Guard patrol vessel recovered both. The Defence Ministry's response chronology lists the time as 16:00.

The area is offshore and outside Romania's territorial sea, in an EEZ-related zone, so the find is not an incursion into Romanian sovereign territory. The debris came from an aerial drone, not a maritime drone. No operator or national attribution has been announced, and the flight or crash date is unknown.
No pyrotechnic hazard was identified. The recovery is separate from beach finds reported on the Romanian coast the same day and from earlier August cases linked to Neptun Deep.

N043.headline: Two drone fragments without explosives found at Câșla Vădanei, Romania
N043.description: On 11 September 2026 bomb-disposal experts assessed two drone fragments on the beach at Câșla Vădanei, Tulcea, Romania, finding no explosives. Origin unknown.
summary: On 11 September 2026 two aerial-drone fragments were found washed ashore on the beach at Câșla Vădanei, between Sulina and Sfântu Gheorghe in Tulcea, Romania. An explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team from the Defence Ministry (MApN) assessed them at 13:30, which is the response time rather than a known crash time, and found no explosive charge.

The Ministry's account gives no operator or national attribution, and the origin of the fragments is unknown. It is not known how many aircraft they came from, and the flight or crash date is unresolved.

N044.headline: Remains of four drones found and neutralised at Edighiol–Periboina, Romania
N044.description: On 11 September 2026 an EOD team found remains of four drones, including an interceptor with explosives, at Edighiol–Periboina, Romania. Origins unknown.
summary: On 11 September 2026, while checking a Coast Guard report, a helicopter-borne explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) team observed several drone wrecks in the Edighiol–Periboina coastal sector of Constanța County, Romania. The remains belonged to four aerial drones, one of them an interceptor drone. The Defence Ministry (MApN) chronology lists the intervention at 17:55.

The cited chronology gives no operator or national attribution for any of the drones. When they flew or came down, and whether they are linked to other drones recovered along the coast, are unresolved.

Explosives were reported specifically on board the interceptor drone. All elements were secured and neutralised in a controlled disposal by the authorities, which is distinct from an explosion during the incident.

N045.headline: Drone fragment with explosives neutralised on Periteașca beach, Romania
N045.description: On 11 September 2026 Border Police found two drone fragments on Periteașca beach, Tulcea, Romania; one held explosives and was neutralised. Origin unknown.
summary: At about 09:30 on 11 September 2026 the Border Police found two drone fragments on Periteașca beach in Tulcea, Romania. The intervention to deal with them is listed at 15:18. The flight or crash date is unknown.

No operator or national attribution has been announced, and the origin of the fragments is unknown. It is not known how many drones they came from, and any link to other drones recovered along the coast is unresolved.

Explosives were confirmed in one of the fragments, and SRI bomb specialists neutralised it in a controlled disposal; the Coast Guard took the other fragment. The find is separate from an earlier case at Gura Portiței on 23 August.

N049.headline: Smuggling drone crashes near Versekėlė, Lithuania, after interception
N049.description: Late on 13 September 2026 a cigarette-smuggling drone from Belarus crashed near Versekėlė, Lithuania, after counter-drone action, border guards said.
summary: Late on the evening of 13 September 2026, Lithuanian border guards detected an inbound cargo drone near Ūta, in the Šalčininkai district on the border with Belarus. Counter-drone action disrupted it; the drone turned back toward the border and crashed in a meadow roughly 500 metres inside Lithuania, near Versekėlė. It was carrying 200 packs of Minsk Superslims cigarettes and a GPS device.

According to the border guard service VSAT, which reported the case on 14 September, the drone was flown by smugglers operating from or across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. It was a criminal cargo flight, not a military attack.
Border guards recovered the broken homemade drone within about an hour and opened administrative proceedings. No casualties or damage to third parties were reported.

N052.headline: Old drone found in forest at Keneliai, Pasvalys district, Lithuania
N052.description: On 16 September 2026 an old drone was reported in a forest at Keneliai, Pasvalys district, Lithuania. Police found no explosives; a foreign origin is unproven.
summary: On 16 September 2026 a drone that appeared to have been lying in vegetation for months was found in a forest at Keneliai village, in Lithuania’s Pasvalys district, and reported to police. The date is that of the discovery and report, not evidence of a flight that day.

Initial speculation that it was a foreign military drone was not confirmed by the later police account. The drone was not identified as a Russian or Ukrainian strike drone, and police later associated it with a smuggling investigation. Its foreign origin has not been publicly established, and how it reached the forest is not known.
ARAS and the military responded to the possible explosive risk. In an update on 17 September, police said no explosives had been found.

N053.headline: Smuggling drone forced down and seized at Norviliškės, Lithuania
N053.description: Shortly after midnight on 16 September 2026 border guards forced down a cigarette-smuggling drone from Belarus at Norviliškės, Lithuania, and seized its cargo.
summary: Shortly after midnight on 16 September 2026, in the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, thermal imaging picked up a drone carrying a rectangular cargo as it entered Lithuania from Belarus near Norviliškės, in the Šalčininkai district. Counter-drone action forced it down, and border guards seized the drone together with 1,000 packs of NZ Gold cigarettes.

According to the border guard service VSAT, the drone was flown by smugglers operating from or across the Belarus border; the operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. It was a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike, and it was brought down by electronic counter-drone measures rather than shot down.
No casualties or third-party damage were reported. Administrative proceedings were opened, and VSAT counted the case as the 57th of the year.

N055.headline: Greece reports Turkish UAV overflight of Zourafa islet in the Aegean
N055.description: On 18 September 2026 Greece’s military said a Turkish UAV flew over Zourafa islet in the northeastern Aegean. The track has not been independently verified.
summary: On 18 September 2026 a UAV flew over Zourafa, an islet in the northeastern Aegean, according to a Greek military account relayed the same day by the Greek outlet Politica. The exact time and the full route were not published, and the drone’s model was not specified.

The Greek account identified the drone as Turkish and presented the overflight as an airspace violation; the track has not been independently verified. The same account reported a formation of manned F-16s over Ro, which is not a drone incident. For the whole day it listed five UAVs among ten aircraft, with 13 flight information region (FIR) infringements and seven airspace violations by mixed aircraft; how many of these involved drones was not specified.
No impact or casualties were reported, and the account did not describe a specific response to the Zourafa overflight.

N059.headline: Intercepted smuggling drone burns near Antaniškės, Lithuania
N059.description: On the night of 21–22 September 2026 a smuggling drone from Belarus burned near Antaniškės, Lithuania, after counter-drone action; its cigarette cargo survived.
summary: On the night of 21–22 September 2026 Lithuanian border guards detected an inbound cargo drone at Liškūniškės, in the Šalčininkai district near the Belarus border. It descended after counter-drone action, and on the morning of 22 September guards found the damaged, scorched drone about 800 metres from the border near Antaniškės. VSAT reported the case on 23 September.

According to the border guard service VSAT, the drone was flown by smugglers operating from or across the Belarus border. The operators’ nationality and any state sponsorship have not been established. It was a criminal cargo flight, not a military strike.

The drone was damaged by its impact and by fire, but its cargo of 1,000 packs of Minsk Superslims cigarettes survived. The drone and cigarettes were seized and administrative proceedings opened; VSAT counted it as the 58th such case of the year. No third-party casualties were reported.

N062.headline: Drone fragments of unknown origin reported on Mamaia Nord beach, Romania
N062.description: Police were notified at about 08:30 on 10 September 2026 of drone fragments on Mamaia Nord beach, Constanța County, Romania. No explosives; origin unknown.
summary: At about 08:30 local time on 10 September 2026 police received a notification about drone fragments on Mamaia Nord beach in Constanța County, on Romania's Black Sea coast. The time is when the police were notified, not a verified crash time.

The operator and origin have not been established in the cited accounts, and the number of aircraft the fragments came from was not specified. The recovery does not show that a drone entered Romanian airspace that day; the original route is unknown.

After examination, no explosive material was reported. The fragments were transferred to the Coast Guard or other competent authorities. The Mamaia Nord find is separate from the Capu Midia discovery the previous evening and from a police notification at Corbu beach at about 09:40 the same morning.

N063.headline: Drone fragments of unknown origin reported on Corbu beach, Romania
N063.description: Police were notified at about 09:40 on 10 September 2026 of drone fragments on Corbu beach, Constanța County, Romania. No explosives; origin unknown.
summary: Police were notified at about 09:40 local time on 10 September 2026 of drone fragments on Corbu beach in Constanța County, on Romania's Black Sea coast. This is the notification time, not a verified crash time.

The cited accounts do not establish an operator or origin, and it is not known how many aircraft the fragments came from. Finding the fragments does not prove a same-day incursion into Romanian airspace, and the route is unknown.

No explosive material was reported after the fragments were examined, and they were handed to the Coast Guard or other competent authorities. The Corbu notification is distinct from the 08:30 report of fragments at Mamaia Nord that morning and from the Capu Midia discovery the evening before.

N064.headline: Suspected drone fragment of unknown origin found at Agigea, Romania
N064.description: On 26 September 2026 fishermen found a suspected drone fragment among coastal blocks at Agigea, Constanța County, Romania. Its origin is unresolved.
summary: On the morning of 26 September 2026 fishermen found a suspected drone fragment among the coastal blocks at Agigea, in Constanța County, Romania, and notified the authorities. Antena 3 CNN described a pale, wing-like object, possibly part of an aerial drone. The date is that of the discovery; when and how the object reached the shore is unknown.

Radio România reported an ongoing investigation. Whether the object is a drone, its model, its origin, its operator and when it was lost have not been established. The discovery alone does not show that a drone crossed into Romania, and it has not been linked to any tracked incursion.

Preliminary reporting showed no attached explosive load, but no final official pyrotechnic assessment had been published. No casualties, damage or detonation were reported, and the reports do not establish that the fragment was physically retrieved.

N065.headline: Reported drone enters Romanian airspace near Chilia Veche, Tulcea
N065.description: Overnight on 26–27 September 2026 radar tracked an aerial target, reported as a drone, entering Romania near Chilia Veche, Tulcea. Its operator is unknown.
summary: During the night of 26–27 September 2026 Romania’s defence ministry reported that an aerial target had entered national airspace near Chilia Veche, in Tulcea County. Radar tracked it for several minutes roughly parallel to the Chilia branch of the Danube before contact was lost near Pardina. The exact time it crossed the border was not stated.

The ministry called it an aerial target; Digi24 reported it as a drone, and its model has not been established. Military radar confirmed a cross-border entry, but the operator and nationality are unresolved, and the ministry release did not attribute it to Russia. Loss of radar contact does not show where the target went, and no crash, shoot-down, explosion or recovery has been confirmed.

Two Spanish F-18s on NATO enhanced air-policing duty and a Romanian IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter took off to monitor it. An RO-Alert warning went out for northern Tulcea County at 23:32, and the alert ended at 00:48 on 27 September. The release gave no casualty or damage assessment.

N066.headline: Unidentified aerial target enters Romania near Ceatalchioi, Tulcea
N066.description: On the evening of 27 September 2026 radar tracked an unidentified aerial target, possibly a drone, from Ceatalchioi to Somova, Romania. Its operator is unknown.
summary: On the evening of 27 September 2026 Romania’s defence ministry reported that an unidentified aerial target had entered Romanian airspace near Ceatalchioi, in Tulcea County. Radar first tracked it over Ukraine north of Chilia Veche; it then followed the border and disappeared from radar about 10 minutes later near Somova. The exact entry time was not given.

Radar confirmed the cross-border entry, but the object’s operator and nationality are unresolved. It was described as a probable drone, but that has not been confirmed, and its type is unknown. Loss of radar contact does not establish a crash, and no shoot-down, explosion or wreckage recovery has been reported.

Two Romanian F-16s took off from Borcea. An RO-Alert warning was issued at 20:35 and the air alert ended at 22:05. A specialist search was announced for the morning of 28 September; its outcome has not been established. The incursion came the evening after a separate aerial target was tracked between Chilia Veche and Pardina.

N067.headline: Possible drone debris found on Insula Mare a Brăilei, Romania
N067.description: On 29 September 2026 fragments of a possible drone were found on Insula Mare a Brăilei, Romania, after a reported fall and fire. Foreign origin is unconfirmed.
summary: Overnight on 28–29 September 2026 a resident called 112 to report a falling object and a fire on arable land on Insula Mare a Brăilei, opposite Gropeni in Brăila County, Romania. Authorities found fragments, and the discovery was reported on the morning of 29 September; the fire had gone out. The exact time of the fall is unknown.

Romania’s defence ministry described the fragments as those of a possible drone; identification and model were pending examination. Foreign origin, operator and nationality are unresolved, and the ministry reported no radar-detected unauthorised entry into Romanian airspace during the preceding night. The reported fall and fire do not establish a confirmed drone crash or explosion.

No casualties or material damage were reported. Interior Ministry and Romanian Intelligence Service teams secured the perimeter, and the defence ministry said a specialist team would examine the area; a completed examination or retrieval had not been reported.

N068.headline: Greece reports two airspace violations by a Turkish UAV in the Aegean
N068.description: On 1 October 2026 Greece’s military reported that one Turkish UAV made two airspace violations and one Athens FIR infringement in the southeastern Aegean.
summary: On 1 October 2026 Greece’s Hellenic National Defence General Staff reported that one Turkish UAV had made two violations of national airspace and one infringement of air-traffic rules in the Athens flight information region (FIR) over the southeastern Aegean. OnAlert relayed the account that evening, followed by NewsIT. No island, coordinates, times or flight track were published.

The Turkish identification and the violation assessment are those of the Greek military, and the flight track has not been independently verified. The drone’s model was not specified. The three figures are different measures of one drone’s activity, not separate aircraft or incidents.
Greek forces reportedly identified and intercepted the UAV. No weapons engagement, shoot-down, crash, casualties or damage were reported.

N069.headline: Possible drone reported falling and starting a fire near Plauru, Romania
N069.description: On 2 October 2026 an object, possibly a drone, was reported falling and starting a fire near Plauru, Tulcea County, Romania. Its foreign origin is unconfirmed.
summary: At about 05:00 on 2 October 2026 Romania’s defence ministry received a report that an object had fallen near Plauru, in Tulcea County, and started a fire. The report came during overnight drone attacks on Ukrainian targets across the Danube. The exact time of the fall and the precise site were not published.

The object was possibly an aerial drone; identification and model were pending technical examination. Its operator, nationality and foreign origin are unresolved. The nearby attacks on Ukraine are context, not attribution, and the ministry recorded no unauthorised entry into Romanian airspace on radar overnight. A fire alone does not establish an explosive payload or detonation.

IGSU firefighters and defence ministry teams were sent to the site, and the area was secured. A specialist examination was announced but not reported as completed. No casualties or material damage were reported. The find is separate from an earlier drone discovery at Plauru in August 2026.

N070.headline: Suspected drone alert in Vilnius County, Lithuania; object not found
N070.description: On 3 October 2026 an unidentified radar contact triggered an air alert and closed Vilnius Airport’s airspace in Lithuania. A drone incursion is unconfirmed.
summary: On the morning of 3 October 2026 an unidentified radar contact led Lithuania to issue a yellow air alert for Vilnius County at 09:48 local time and to close Vilnius Airport’s controlled airspace temporarily. The all-clear followed at 10:34. The object was first reported as entering from Belarus; officials later described a track toward Vilnius and Ukmergė that vanished before reaching Vilnius.

It has not been established that the object was a drone. Officials said the unusually slow track could represent birds or a radar anomaly, and a foreign drone incursion remains unconfirmed. An approach from Belarus does not establish Belarusian or Russian responsibility, and no operator or nationality has been identified.

NATO fighters did not locate the object, and a Lithuanian Air Force helicopter found nothing suspicious; the search ended around 13:00. No wreckage, casualties or damage were confirmed, and reports of a possible fire or explosion were not substantiated.

N071.headline: Greece reports six airspace violations by two Turkish UAVs in Aegean
N071.description: On 4 October 2026 Greece’s military reported six airspace violations and three FIR infringements by two Turkish UAVs in the northeastern and central Aegean.
summary: On 4 October 2026 Greece’s Hellenic National Defence General Staff reported that two Turkish UAVs had been active over the northeastern and central Aegean, recording six violations of national airspace and three infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR). OnAlert relayed the account that evening; exact sites and sortie times were not published.

The Turkish identification and the description of the flights as national-airspace violations are Greek military assessments, and the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute remains relevant. The drones’ models were not specified, and no coordinates or tracks have been independently verified. The figures measure different things and are not separate incidents.
The drones were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No armed aircraft, engagements, shoot-downs, crashes, casualties or damage were reported.

N072.headline: Fatal drone attack reported on grain ship Royad Mammadov off Romania
N072.description: On 5 October 2026 drones reportedly struck the grain ship Royad Mammadov in Romania’s Black Sea EEZ. Accounts of the dead conflict; Ukraine blamed Russia.
summary: On 5 October 2026 the grain carrier Royad Mammadov, sailing from Izmail in Ukraine to Ravenna in Italy, was damaged by a reported drone strike, an onboard blast and fire in the Black Sea near the Pescăruș platform, about 30 nautical miles south of Sfântu Gheorghe. The site was in Romania’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ), outside its territorial waters. A rescue request was logged at 10:37 local time; the exact strike time is not verified.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said two Russian drones struck the ship. That is a Ukrainian claim, not independent verification, and Romania has published no attribution finding. Marius Roibu, director of the MRCC Constanța rescue centre, described an apparent multiple-drone attack; the drones’ type, launch point and operators are unestablished.

Casualty accounts conflict. Romania’s Interior Ministry initially reported two dead and eleven rescued; on 6 October Azerbaijan’s Foreign Ministry said the captain had been killed and another Azerbaijani crew member was missing. India’s embassy said three Indian crew members survived, one of them injured. An initial report that the ship sank was corrected on 6 October, when it was reported afloat and awaiting a tow to Midia. Petrom said the Pescăruș platform was unaffected.

N073.headline: Drone attack off Bulgaria sinks ALFA WATAN and sets ABLE on fire
N073.description: Early on 6 October 2026 drones attacked two merchant ships in Bulgaria’s Black Sea EEZ east of Byala, sinking ALFA WATAN. Bulgaria has not attributed it.
summary: In the early hours of 6 October 2026 two merchant ships, the Togo-flagged ALFA WATAN and the Palau-flagged ABLE, were attacked about 70 nautical miles east of Byala, in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone outside its territorial waters. Bulgarian authorities reported aerial and maritime attack drones. ALFA WATAN sank, and the nearby ferry DIOSCURIA witnessed an explosion; ABLE caught fire.

Bulgaria has not attributed the attack. Rumen Radev said on 7 October that the circumstances suggested Russia but the evidence was insufficient for definitive attribution; Russia denied targeting the vessel. On 6 October Zelensky alleged a combined Russian attack, citing a joint investigation; that is a Ukrainian claim, not a Bulgarian finding. On 9 October Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov assessed ABLE’s damage as a surface-drone strike, without naming an operator.

ALFA WATAN’s crew are missing, not confirmed dead. Reuters reported twelve Syrians missing on 7 October, then ten missing, including nine Syrians, on 8 October; the discrepancy is unresolved. All eighteen ABLE crew were rescued, two of them injured. Bulgaria halted the search on 7 October, and on 8 October Syria sought an independent investigation. A 9 October inspection found no identifiable drone remnants aboard ABLE, which was still afloat.

NOVA reported on 20 October that ABLE had sunk off Turkey after disappearing from radar late on 19 October. The ship had left Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone on 14 October. This reported later sinking remains a follow-up to the 6 October attack; no direct wreck survey or exact sinking position was retrieved.

N074.headline: Greece reports nine airspace violations by four Turkish UAVs in Aegean
N074.description: On 6 October 2026 Greece’s military reported four Turkish UAVs over the Aegean, with nine national-airspace violations and seven Athens FIR infringements.
summary: On 6 October 2026 a Greek military (GEETHA) bulletin, reproduced that evening by Liberal, reported four Turkish UAVs over the northeastern and southeastern Aegean. It recorded nine violations of national airspace and seven infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR) by the drones. Exact sites and sortie times were not published.

The Turkish identification is GEETHA’s, and the assessment that the flights violated national airspace remains Greece’s, given the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute. No flight tracks have been independently verified. The bulletin also listed two manned F-16s and a CN-235, which are excluded from the drone figures; it described the F-16s, not the UAVs, as armed.

The UAVs were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No shoot-down, weapons engagement, crash, casualties or damage were reported. The figures count different things and are not separate incidents.

N075.headline: Greece reports four airspace violations by three Turkish UAVs in Aegean
N075.description: On 7 October 2026 Greece’s military reported that three Turkish UAVs made four airspace violations and three Athens FIR infringements over the Aegean.
summary: On the evening of 7 October 2026 OnAlert published a Greek military (GEETHA) account of three Turkish UAVs over the northeastern, central and southeastern Aegean that day. According to that account, the drones made four violations of national airspace and three infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR). Exact sites and sortie times were not published.

The Turkish identification is GEETHA’s, and the national-airspace violation assessment remains Greece’s, given the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute. No flight tracks or boundary assessments have been independently verified. The drones’ models, armament and payload were not established.

The UAVs were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No armed aircraft, engagements, shoot-downs, crashes, casualties or damage were reported. The three figures count different things and are not separate incidents.

N076.headline: Greece reports five airspace violations by five Turkish UAVs in Aegean
N076.description: On 8 October 2026 Greece’s military reported five Turkish UAVs over the Aegean, with five national-airspace violations and five Athens FIR infringements.
summary: On 8 October 2026 a Greek military (GEETHA) account, published that evening by Dimokratiki and NewsIT, reported five Turkish UAVs over the northeastern and southeastern Aegean. It recorded five violations of national airspace and five infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR) by the drones. Exact sites and sortie times were not published.

The Turkish identification is GEETHA’s, and the national-airspace violation assessment remains Greece’s, given the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute. No flight tracks have been independently verified. A manned ATR-72 in the same bulletin accounted for two further FIR infringements, which are not part of the drone figures.

The UAVs were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No shoot-down, weapons engagement, crash, casualties or damage were reported. The figures count different things and are not separate incidents.

N077.headline: UAV debris of unknown origin destroyed at sea off Sinemorets, Bulgaria
N077.description: On 9 October 2026 Bulgaria’s Navy destroyed floating drone fragments 15 nautical miles east of Sinemorets in a controlled detonation. Their origin is unknown.
summary: Around midday on 9 October 2026 floating parts of an aerial drone were spotted in the Black Sea, reportedly 15 nautical miles east of Sinemorets, off Bulgaria. The Bulgarian Navy sent the minehunter Struma to examine them. The date is that of the discovery; when the drone originally came down is not known.

The fragments have not been identified beyond being from a UAV, and the model and number of aircraft are unknown. Their origin, operator and nationality have not been established, and no Russian or Ukrainian attribution has been confirmed. There is no evidence linking them to the 6 October drone attack on the merchant ships ALFA WATAN and ABLE.

Explosive material was suspected but not confirmed. Divers from the auxiliary ship Kapitan I rang Dimitar Dobrev recommended destroying the debris in place, and the Navy commander authorised a controlled detonation. No casualties or vessel damage were reported.

N078.headline: Greece reports five airspace violations by six Turkish UAVs in Aegean
N078.description: On 10 October 2026 Greece’s military reported six Turkish UAVs over the Aegean, with five national-airspace violations and eight Athens FIR infringements.
summary: On 10 October 2026 Greece’s military (GEETHA) reported six Turkish military UAVs over the northeastern, central and southeastern Aegean, with five violations of national airspace and eight infringements of the Athens flight information region (FIR). OnAlert published the account that evening, and DefenceNet repeated it early on 11 October; both describe the same day’s activity.

The Turkish identification and the national-airspace assessment are GEETHA’s, and the Greek-Turkish airspace dispute remains relevant. No tracks or boundary assessments have been independently verified. Models, armament and payload were not established.

The drones were identified and intercepted under standard procedures. No shoot-down, weapons engagement, crash, casualties or damage were reported. The figures count different things and are not separate incidents.

N079.headline: Bulgaria reports drone strike on ship CHELSEA 3 off Byala; crew rescued
N079.description: Bulgaria said drones struck the ship CHELSEA 3 east of Byala overnight on 13 October 2026; all 15 crew were rescued. The operator has not been identified.
summary: Overnight on 13 October 2026 the Maltese-flagged merchant ship CHELSEA 3 was struck by drones in the Black Sea, reportedly 18 nautical miles east of Byala in Varna Province, within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone and outside its territorial waters. According to the crew’s account, relayed by Bulgaria’s prime minister, three aerial drones hit the deck and hull. A distress notification reached Varna’s maritime rescue centre at 01:30 local time.

The operator and nationality are unresolved. Radev said the evidence was insufficient to accuse either belligerent; he argued that the attacks benefit Russia, but that argument and planned diplomatic consultations do not establish Russian responsibility. The ship is reportedly Ukrainian-owned and registered in Odessa, which is separate from the question of who attacked it.

Border Police evacuated all 15 crew, seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, who were brought to Varna; five were treated for initially reported minor injuries, and no deaths were reported. BNR reports that the damaged ship docked at Burgas-West on 17 October; the investigation remains open. On 13 October, another vessel was reported struck and sunk east of Krapets.
MaltaDaily’s account gives 12 October and four minor injuries. Those differences from the Bulgarian account remain unresolved and do not identify a second attack.

On 19 October, Burgas maritime administration director Zhivko Petrov assessed the three hull breaches as blast damage, possibly from a surface drone. This conflicts with the initial aerial-drone account and remains subject to specialist investigation. The vessel was stable in port and a military-prosecutor investigation was underway.

On 20 October, the prime minister reported examination of drone remains and chemical analysis to identify the explosive used. Allied specialists were expected the following day. No final weapon identification or operator finding was announced; the transport minister did not specify the fragments’ nature or recovery location.

N080.headline: HS Dignity identified as ship sunk off Krapets; eleven sailors missing
N080.description: HS Dignity sank in a reported drone attack off Krapets, Bulgaria, on 13 October 2026. Five sailors were rescued and eleven were missing; attribution is unresolved.
summary: The merchant ship reported struck by a drone and sunk off Krapets on 13 October 2026 has been identified as HS Dignity, sailing under the Guinea-Bissau flag. The reported location, about 17 nautical miles east of Krapets, is in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, outside territorial waters. The exact strike and sinking times remain unpublished.

Later reporting gives five sailors rescued and eleven missing, replacing the initial account of one rescue. Search-and-rescue operations continued at the time of that reporting. The missing sailors are not counted as confirmed dead. The identification and rescue update concern the same sinking, not another attack.

The drone’s type and operator remain unresolved. Ukraine accused Russia, but Bulgarian authorities have not established responsibility conclusively. The vessel’s flag does not identify its crew’s nationalities. This incident remains separate from the CHELSEA 3 attack near Byala and the 6 October attacks on ALFA WATAN and ABLE.

N081.headline: Karwia beach wreckage identified as a Polish test drone; excluded from register
N081.description: The drone wreckage found at Karwia, Poland, on 13 October 2026 was identified as a Polish test drone. This domestic case is excluded from foreign-drone totals.
summary: Poland’s defence minister identified the wreckage found on Karwia beach on 13 October 2026 as a Polish test drone. He said it had been destroyed during drone and counter-drone exercises near Ustka several weeks earlier, and that the sea later washed its fragments ashore.

The discovery was initially recorded here as an unidentified candidate because its origin was unresolved. The official domestic identification reported on 14 October resolves that question. On review on 15 October, the record was removed from the map, replay and foreign-drone totals.

This page keeps its original address and sources so readers can see the correction. The discovery date remains 13 October; the earlier training destruction is not a new shoot-down on that date. The exact drone model and test date were not disclosed in the reviewed reports.

N082.headline: Romania issues northern Tulcea RO-Alert; no airspace entry detected
N082.description: Romania issued a northern Tulcea RO-Alert on 14 October 2026. Three aerial targets remained over Ukraine; MApN reported no entry into Romanian airspace.
summary: Romania issued a RO-Alert warning for northern Tulcea County at 06:39 on 14 October 2026 after radar detected three aerial targets near Vâlkove, Ukraine. Two Romanian F-16 fighters and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter were deployed.

The Defence Ministry explicitly stated that none of the three targets entered Romanian national airspace. The statement did not establish their models or operator, and three aerial targets should not be read as three confirmed drones.

The register includes this as one civil-protection alert and response, not a foreign incursion. No strike, shoot-down, casualties, damage or wreckage were reported. Its map marker represents the Romanian warning area, not a drone position.

N083.headline: Aerial target enters Romania near Sulina, then is shot down in Ukraine
N083.description: A target briefly entered Romanian airspace east of Sulina on 14 October 2026, then was shot down in Ukraine. Drone identity and operator remain unresolved.
summary: Romania’s Defence Ministry reported a brief morning incursion east of Sulina on 14 October 2026. A 10:19 RO-Alert warned residents in northern and eastern Tulcea, and two Romanian F-16s launched. Exact entry time was not given.

The unidentified target returned to Ukrainian airspace, where Ukrainian air defence shot it down, according to the ministry. The Romanian map marker identifies the incursion area, not the later shoot-down site. Its UAV identity and operator remain unresolved.
The all-clear came at 11:22. This is separate from the 06:39 alert that involved no Romanian entry and from the afternoon and evening incursions. No Romanian casualties or damage were reported.

N084.headline: Aerial target spends eight minutes in Romanian airspace northeast of Sulina
N084.description: An unidentified aerial target entered Romanian airspace northeast of Sulina from 17:38 to 17:46 on 14 October 2026. Its operator and UAV identity are unresolved.
summary: Romanian radar tracked an unidentified target entering national airspace at 17:38 on 14 October 2026, about 22 km northeast of Sulina over territorial waters. It departed at 17:46.
Two Romanian F-16s launched and a RO-Alert was issued at 17:39. The air alert ended at 19:03. No weapons engagement, shoot-down, damage or casualties were reported.
This is a separate afternoon incursion. The official statement establishes the crossing and duration, while identification as a UAV, its model and operator remain unresolved.

N085.headline: Two aerial targets enter Romania off Tulcea; one later destroyed near Reni
N085.description: Two targets entered Romanian airspace at 20:04 on 14 October 2026. One vanished from radar at sea; the other was later destroyed in Ukraine. Attribution is unknown.
summary: Two aerial targets entered Romanian airspace over the Black Sea at 20:04 on 14 October 2026, according to the Defence Ministry. Contact with one was lost over the sea; the other left at 20:13 toward Vâlcove and was later destroyed by Ukrainian air defence near Reni.
Two Spanish F-18s launched. Warnings were issued for Tulcea at 20:02 and eastern Galați at 20:33; the all-clear came at 21:14. The targets’ models and operators remain unresolved.

Both targets are retained in one timed incursion record. Radar loss does not prove a crash or a strike on YARA J, whose separate incident is recorded as N086. A connection remains unproven, and the records should not be interpreted as a verified count of distinct drones.

N086.headline: Drone strike sets YARA J on fire near Sulina; crew safe
N086.description: YARA J was hit near Sulina on 14 October 2026. Its 17 crew were safe. A NATO military source assessed the drones as Russian in origin.
summary: A drone struck the Comoros-flagged tanker YARA J near Sulina on 14 October 2026. Romania’s president confirmed the attack the next day. A NATO military source cited by Reuters assessed the drones that hit YARA J and WINE TRADER as Russian in origin; a specific operator has not been established in the reviewed reporting.

The crew reported an explosion and fire. The fire was extinguished and all reported 17 crew were safe, with no injuries or sinking reported. The vessel was inside Romanian territorial waters. MRCC requested assistance at 20:25; SAR Apollo departed at 20:31 and was recalled at 21:30 after the crew said help was no longer needed. These are rescue times, not a verified strike time.

This updates the original incident and retains its URL. The initial absence of a radar-detected approach does not undo the later attack confirmation. A connection to the 20:04 radar episode in N085 remains unproven. WINE TRADER and Sea Destiny have separate records.

N087.headline: Drone briefly enters Romanian airspace southeast of Sulina at 01:34
N087.description: Romania’s Defence Ministry reported a drone in national airspace southeast of Sulina at 01:34 on 15 October 2026. It vanished from radar; its operator is unknown.
summary: A drone was detected in Romanian airspace over territorial waters southeast of Sulina at 01:34 on 15 October 2026. The Defence Ministry said it remained visible for about one minute before disappearing from radar.

Spanish F-18s launched during the overnight alert. Romanian F-16s were later deployed for other contacts farther east of Snake Island, followed by a 04:57 warning. The release reported no further entries and an all-clear at 05:46.

This is a separate post-midnight incursion. The drone’s model and operator are unknown. Loss of radar contact does not establish a shoot-down, crash or impact; none was confirmed in the reviewed statement.

N088.headline: Greece reports six Turkish UAVs and four airspace violations in Aegean
N088.description: Greece reported six Turkish UAVs, four airspace violations and eleven FIR infringements on 15 October 2026. No weapons engagement was reported.
summary: Greece’s military reported six Turkish UAVs over the northeastern and southeastern Aegean on 15 October 2026. NewsIT and ProtoThema reproduced four national-airspace violations and eleven Athens FIR infringements. All six aircraft were identified and intercepted, with no weapons engagement reported.

The aircraft models, exact sites and sortie times were not published. Turkish attribution and the national-airspace assessment are those of Greek authorities; the latter remains subject to the longstanding Greek-Turkish airspace dispute. The original GEETHA bulletin was not retrieved directly.
No crashes, casualties, damage or EOD operations were reported. This is one dated activity record. UAV, violation and FIR counts measure different things and do not create additional incident rows.

N089.headline: Sea Destiny reports nearby explosion after NATO names it as targeted ship
N089.description: NATO named Sea Destiny as targeted near Sulina overnight on 14–15 October 2026. The ship reported a nearby explosion but no damage; the cause is unresolved.
summary: NATO named the Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier Sea Destiny as an additional targeted ship during the 14–15 October incidents near Sulina. Romania’s defence minister said it reported an explosion within visual range but was unaffected. The vessel was reported inside Romanian territorial waters.

The incident remains provisional. A drone-caused explosion, a hit on the ship and its operator have not been confirmed. The Russian-origin assessment reported for the drones that struck YARA J and WINE TRADER is not specifically an attribution for Sea Destiny. No damage, casualties, recovery or EOD operation was reported.

The exact explosion time and location remain unpublished. Replay uses 14 October, the first day of the overnight range. This record remains separate from the two tankers; Dania J at Izmail, Ukraine, is outside the register’s EU scope.

N090.headline: Drone strike sets WINE TRADER on fire off Sulina; seven crew missing
N090.description: WINE TRADER was hit off Sulina on 15 October 2026; five crew were rescued and seven missing. A NATO source assessed the drones as Russian in origin.
summary: A drone struck the San Marino-flagged tanker WINE TRADER off Sulina on 15 October 2026. Romania’s president confirmed the attack. A NATO military source cited by Reuters assessed the drones that hit this tanker and YARA J as Russian in origin; a specific operator has not been established in the reviewed reporting.

Of twelve crew, five were rescued and seven remained missing. Two survivors had scalp burns or mild smoke inhalation; all five were stable and taken to hospital. Fire damaged the vessel. Its final condition is unconfirmed, and the missing crew are not counted as confirmed dead. Heavy seas hindered the continuing rescue operation. IGSU reported that the search resumed on 16 October; its initial boarding announcement was a plan. A 19 October seafarers union statement subsequently reported that teams had boarded and searched accessible spaces, with damage hindering the search. The union reiterated five rescued and seven missing.

N096.headline: Drone explosion near Juodžionys damages a passing car
N096.description: A drone entered Lithuania on 18 October and exploded near Juodžionys, damaging a car. Officials identified Ukrainian origin; a joint investigation continues.
summary: A drone entered Lithuania on the morning of 18 October 2026 and reportedly exploded near Juodžionys in Pasvalys district. Debris damaged a passing car without injuring its occupants. The precise sequence of the explosion and fall remained under investigation.

Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas linked the craft to Ukraine’s attack on St Petersburg and assessed that Russian electronic warfare had diverted it. On 19 October, Lithuania’s prime minister said wreckage and Ukraine’s notification supported Ukrainian origin and that the drone carried explosives. Poland’s defence ministry also identified it as Ukrainian and denied the claim that it had launched from Lithuania. The jamming explanation remained an assessment.

Lithuania’s published chronology puts first radar contact at 05:47 EEST over Poland and entry into Lithuania at 06:02. Polish radar did not independently corroborate that track. NATO fighters scrambled but did not shoot. Latvian surveillance did not indicate entry into Latvia; unverified Polish reports are not additional confirmed occurrences.
On 20 October, President Nausėda said the Lithuanian and Polish defence ministries had formed a joint investigation group. The full route and crash mechanism remained unresolved.
